Same for giving a teacher an existing role string: RepPolicy/StaffPolicy handlers would read Id() as a student or admin id. Teacher endpoints must be separate and teacher role strings new.

GET /api/auth/session falls through to AdminUsers for anything that is not a student (AuthEndpoints.cs:339-340). If the ValidateAsync branch ships without this fix, a teacher either gets a 500 on every page load or is shown as the dashboard account with the same row number.

Pending teachers. Item 2 says a teacher waiting for approval may only view. Role is recomputed per request, which is good, but every teacher write endpoint has to be on LinkedTeacherPolicy, not just TeacherPolicy; one missed endpoint lets an unapproved person cancel classes and notify students. Item 3 (picking other courses/sections) widens this: if a picked section carries change powers, any staff address can cancel any class.

Test mode. If a server is ever run with Auth:TestMode on and the teacher code were shown like a student's (AuthEndpoints.cs:162), anyone could type a lecturer's address, be auto-linked by name and cancel classes with live notifications. The teacher endpoint must never return testCode; the consequence is that teacher sign-in only works where real email works.

Email to staff mailboxes is untested. Codes are sent from an outside domain through Resend; delivery was only ever confirmed to student mailboxes. If the staff mail system filters it, no teacher can sign in and there is no fallback (no password, no on-screen code). 'Live for everyone at once' depends on this.

Mail abuse and shared quota. Anyone who knows /teach can make Classy send a code email to any @gutech.edu.om address: 4 per 15 min per browser, 20 a day per address (LoginCodes.cs:14-25), and up to 1000 requests per 5 min per IP (Program.cs:89). Staff addresses are guessable, mistyped ones bounce (hurting the sender reputation students' sign-in depends on), and the same Resend account sends students' codes.

Lock-out by a stranger. The 20-codes and 30-wrong-codes daily caps are per address across all browsers (AuthEndpoints.cs:122-130): someone can use up a teacher's allowance so the teacher cannot sign in on a new device that day. Devices the teacher already used are exempt (trusted-device cookie), the same trade-off students have today.

Trusted-device list is shared. unischedule-device holds at most 5 keys per browser across students, dashboard accounts and now teacher emails (SignInCookies.cs:20, 52); on a shared office PC a sixth sign-in pushes the oldest out and that person loses the exemptions there. Minor.

Removal does not stick. Sign-in creates the account on first verify (AuthEndpoints.cs:219-225 for students). If teachers work the same way, 'remove a teacher' (item 11) signs them out, but they can sign straight back in and be auto-linked again by their email unless a block is stored.

Notifications to the wrong person. Push subscriptions are per device endpoint and only dropped on a proper logout (AuthEndpoints.cs:319-323, session.tsx:40-45). Signing in at /teach on top of a student session (or the reverse) replaces the cookie but leaves the previous person's subscription on that device unless /teach signs the old session out first.

Client guards send teachers to the wrong login. Today StudentOnly, StaffOnly, Join and Planner all end at /login or /admin/login for any kind they do not know (main.tsx:43, 53; Join.tsx:42; Planner.tsx:18). Missing one leaves a signed-in teacher looking at the student ID screen, which cannot accept an email (digits only, Login.tsx:19-23).

Existing tests are tightly coupled to the student contract: ~20 files post { universityId } and read testCode, and SignInSafetyTests assert on message wording. Refactoring request-code/verify into shared helpers must keep the student request, response and messages byte-for-byte.
Production has real students and migrations must stay additive: making PushSubscription.StudentId nullable would rebuild the table in SQLite; a separate teacher table avoids that.

A 60-day sliding sign-in (Program.cs:57-58) on a shared office or classroom computer now carries the power to cancel and move classes; there is no 'sign out everywhere' for code-based accounts (only dashboard accounts have SessionVersion).
openProductQuestions: New item 3: when a teacher adds a course or section that is not under their name, is that only for seeing it on their timetable, or can they also cancel, move and change the room for it? When an owner or RSA removes a teacher, should that email be blocked from signing in again? If not, the person can simply sign in again and, if their email matches a name, be linked again at once.

Teacher sign-in will only ever work by email (the code is never shown on screen, same as for owners). Nobody has yet tested whether Classy's code emails reach staff mailboxes. Who has a staff address that can try it before launch, and should launch wait for that test?

Anyone who knows the /teach address can make Classy send a sign-in code email to any staff address (up to 20 a day per address). Is that acceptable, or should Classy only email addresses that match a name on the timetable or that an owner has added?
A browser can hold only one Classy sign-in. A person who is both dashboard staff (RSA or owner) and a teacher, or an owner who is a student, has to sign out of one to use the other. Is that fine?

Do all GUtech teaching staff have exactly one address in the firstname.lastname@gutech.edu.om form? A teacher who signs in with a second address or alias would become a second, separate teacher account.

risks: Hand-picked sections plus 'changes are live at once with no approval' means any signed-in teacher could add any section in the university and cancel or move it. Nothing in the model limits a change to sections under the teacher's approved name. This is the main security question raised by the new request.

Combined classes: in the real EduWave data 122 groups of 2-3 sections with different course codes share the same teacher, time, room and dates (18 of 91 teachers). Per-section overlays would let a teacher cancel BE 1 101 while IBSM 1 101 and LOG 1 101 students still see the class; the teacher's own timetable would show three stacked blocks flagged as a clash (slots.ts:131 only ignores same-course pairs; Clashes.Find at Dtos.cs:82-89 flags them); the 'room is taken' check would report the teacher's own sibling section; class size would be a third of the real room.

One class per course is assumed across the web (Course.tsx:17, Lab.tsx:620, Session.tsx:28, slots.ts:113 and 131, absences.ts:65/108, the /course/{courseId} route, reminder links ?session={courseId}.date.time at Notifications.cs:202). 26 of 91 teachers teach several sections of one course, so reusing the student pages unchanged would open the wrong section, merge sessions and hide real clashes between a teacher's two sections of the same course.

Meeting ids are not stable (ScheduleImport.cs:417-418, AdminEndpoints.cs:335-336): any overlay keyed on Meeting.Id is silently orphaned by the next sync. Calendar UIDs already churn for the same reason (CalendarFeed.cs:185).

Reusing the planner fingerprint as-is (PlannerEngine.cs:17) would drop a teacher's change when EduWave changes only the room or end time, and would do so silently (PublishedAsync 199-202 just filters), contradicting 'the teacher is told'.

Section.ChangedAt/ChangeSummary is one slot per section: a teacher change and an EduWave change close together overwrite each other's summary; the push tag change-{sectionId} (Notifications.cs:253) replaces the earlier notification on the device; publishing a semester wipes all of them (AdminEndpoints.cs:68-69). If a teacher endpoint stamps ChangedAt outside the transaction-first pattern, the worker's cursor (Notifications.cs:379-385) can skip the alert.

Today a cancelled session disappears (excludedDates -> onDate false). The agreed 'stays greyed out and marked Cancelled' needs a new shape; if the greyed block is fed through the normal session list it will count in clashes, 'next class', reminders, absence totals and free-time search. It must stay out of StudentSchedule items and exist only as a display record.

Privacy: class size is the count of Picks, which in practice can be 1-3 (the dev data shows mostly 1). A clash count of '1 of 1' for a proposed time tells the teacher that one identifiable student is busy then, and with own slots included it leaks private slots (GroupEndpoints.cs:152-156 deliberately shows those only as 'Busy'). Picks also include students who never finished setup, so the number is not enrolment.

Teachers must not see notes: the shared builder currently always attaches note counts (StudentEndpoints.cs:340-346, 363). The teacher path must skip VisibleNotes entirely, not return zeros computed from someone's picks.

Every student-owned table has a non-null StudentId FK (CustomSlot, PushSubscription, Absence; AppDb.cs:151-168) and StudentSchedule.Item, Busy and reminders are keyed by StudentId. Putting teachers in as fake Students would make them appear in student counts, analytics and class sizes; a separate owner key is needed and ids must not collide in dictionaries keyed by int (Busy.cs:28, Notifications.cs:177).

Cost: StudentSchedule.ForAsync loads all picks, sections and meetings for the given students (70-72) and PublishedAsync loads every section of the semester (PlannerEngine.cs:199). A clash count for a 60-student section with dated meetings is thousands of rows per call; fine on demand, not on every keystroke of a time picker. Adding an overlay query to every /me/timetable needs the index.

Instructor matching is by text. If EduWave renames or replaces the instructor on a section, the section silently leaves the teacher's timetable (and joins someone else's); their active changes on future sessions would then belong to nobody who can undo them except staff.

A section dropped by a sync is deleted (ScheduleImport.cs:367-368). With a cascading FK the teacher's changes and hand-picked rows vanish with it and the dashboard log loses history; with no FK handling the delete fails. Needs explicit ending plus snapshots.

Days off and term edges: a weekly class has no session on a day off (StudentSchedule.cs:32-33), so 'cancel/move that session' must be refused there; a class moved onto a day off is a dated session and would happen (same rule as dated classes), which may surprise.

Old cached web bundles and the offline timetable copy (timetable.tsx:34-42) will not know the changes array: they will hide a cancelled class and miss a moved one until the app updates. Acceptable only because rollout is all at once; the server must keep excludedDates correct for them.
Public timetable API and CSV export stay on the raw timetable, so an outside consumer of /api/public/timetable will still list a class a teacher cancelled.
openProductQuestions: When a teacher adds a course or section that is not under their name: can they also cancel, move and change rooms for it, or only see it on their timetable? Does a hand-added section make that teacher show up for students (on the class page, on the teacher's page under 'classes they teach', with their office hours), or is it private to the teacher's own timetable while students keep seeing the name from EduWave?

The student 'Changed' badge is one per class and clears when the student opens the class. Is that enough for teacher changes, together with the Cancelled/Moved mark on the session itself, or should each changed session stay marked as new until seen?

DATA (server/UniSchedule.Api/Planner/PlannerModels.cs)
- PlannerEvent (35-43): Id, SemesterId, Version (concurrency token, Data/AppDb.cs 73-77), PayloadJson (one EventSpec), Withdrawn, UpdatedAt. It has NO author, NO workspace and NO section column.
- EventSpec (86-87): Kind exam|class, Action add|replace|cancel, Title, Date, Start, End, Room, Targets[], RepeatUntil?, Source?, Notes?. PlannerSource (85): CourseId, SectionId, Fingerprint, Date, Start, End. PlannerTarget (84): CourseId + SectionIds (empty = every section).
- PlannerProposal (45-56) is the draft (belongs to a workspace, optional EventId + BaseEventVersion). PlannerActivity (58-69) is the history; WorkspaceId is required with a cascade FK (AppDb.cs 84-87).

HOW A CLASS SESSION IS IDENTIFIED
- PlannerEngine.Fingerprint (Planner/PlannerEngine.cs:17) = SHA-256 of "CourseId|SectionId|Day|Start|End|Room|Date", invariant culture (test PlannerTests.cs 489-504). It is content-based because Meeting.Id is not stable: ScheduleImport.ApplyAsync (Schedule/ScheduleImport.cs 414-418) deletes and recreates every meeting row of a section whenever anything about that section changed, including an instructor-only change.
- One session = (fingerprint, original date). For dated meetings the date is inside the hash, so the fingerprint alone names one session; for weekly meetings the fingerprint names the weekly pattern and Source.Date picks the week (Validate, PlannerEngine.cs 59).
- It survives a re-import only while course id, section id, weekday, start, end, room and date are all unchanged. Courses are matched by Code (ScheduleImport.cs 384) and sections by Number (402), so ids normally survive. It breaks on: a room-only change, any time change, a section that disappears from one upload and returns later (DropSection 352-369 deletes it, new Section.Id), a course removed and re-added. Instructor is NOT part of it.

STALENESS IS COMPUTED AT READ TIME, NEVER STORED
- PublishedAsync (PlannerEngine.cs 194-203) loads every non-withdrawn event of the semester plus every section and meeting, rebuilds the whole fingerprint set and drops events whose Source.Fingerprint is missing. Returns early with no cost when there are no events (197).
- Effect: the adjustment silently lapses and students see the university class again (PlannerTests.cs 127-145). Nobody is notified. If the timetable later reverts, the adjustment silently comes back to life. Reps only see a "stale" card in their calendar (PlannerEngine.cs 124, 135; web/src/planner/Calendar.tsx 17).

AUDIENCES AND THE STUDENT VIEW
- PublishedPlan.For(picks) (PlannerEngine.cs 222-245): an event reaches a student when a pick has the target's CourseId and the target's SectionIds is empty or contains the pick's SectionId (228). No roster, no major/year.
- Per week from Weeks() (77-91): with a Source, the original date is added to excluded[fingerprint] (232-237); if shown and not a cancel, one PlannerOccurrence is emitted (238-241), once per event even when several picks match (matching[0], 239).
- So cancel = exclusion only; replace = exclusion + a new dated occurrence; add = occurrence only.
- Two separate consumers build the student view: (a) Schedule/StudentSchedule.cs ForAsync (67-100) sets Item.Skip from excluded (81-83) and adds Source.Planner items (87-93); it feeds CalendarFeed.cs 127/180, reminders (Students/Notifications.cs 177), Busy.cs 26 (groups), Absences.cs 73. (b) GET /me/timetable does its own version (Students/StudentEndpoints.cs 322-337, 352): meetings get excludedDates (merged with days off) plus a plannerEvents list.
- Web: lib/slots.ts onDate (177-182) returns false for an excluded date, so a cancelled or moved class simply VANISHES. plannerEvents become sessions labelled "Published by a batch representative" (slots.ts 112-119). There is no "Cancelled" or "Moved" mark anywhere today.
- Publishing sends no push: Notifications.Changes (Notifications.cs 234-255) only reads Section.ChangedAt.

WHAT Enabled() GATES (PlannerEngine.cs 22-24: AppSettings "planner.enabled" overrides config Planner:Enabled, default false)
- The whole /api/rep group for non-owners (PlannerEndpoints.cs 78-84). Owners bypass it, so owner-preview events can exist in the database while the planner is off.
- The AI worker for non-owners (PlannerAi.cs 93).
- Every student-facing read: timetable (StudentEndpoints.cs 322), Absences.cs 73, CalendarFeed.cs 69/88, GroupEndpoints.cs 133/185, the reminder worker (Notifications.cs 349), FreeRooms.cs 60, session notes (PersonalEndpoints.cs 71).
- The menu link (StudentEndpoints.cs 148, web/src/student/StudentShell.tsx 38).
- Tests pin "off hides rep changes": PlannerTests.cs 92-94, 251-254, 284-289.

DRAFTS VS PUBLISHED REVISIONS
- Saving a proposal (PlannerEndpoints.cs 176-201) never touches PlannerEvent. Analyze (PlannerEngine.cs 140-191) returns conflicts plus a token hashing the spec, thresholds and calendar.
- Publish (PlannerEndpoints.cs 213-244), in one transaction: proposal version check, re-validate, re-analyze and compare token, explanation required when there are warnings, event Version must equal BaseEventVersion (225), OwnsEvent (43-45: the workspace of the first "published" activity; owners may change any), then a rule allowing only ONE published adjustment per university occurrence (227-236), then create the event or bump Version and overwrite PayloadJson.
- Withdraw (250-260) sets Withdrawn and needs an explanation. Drafts appear only in the workspace calendar (PlannerEngine.cs 115-119).

VERDICT
Teacher changes should be a SEPARATE overlay table that reuses the fingerprint function and the "events + excluded dates" output shape, not rows in PlannerEvent. Reasons from the code: every delivery path is switched off by Enabled(); the publish flow is draft -> analysis token -> publish with ownership derived from a workspace; the one-adjustment-per-occurrence rule conflicts with "teacher wins"; staleness is silent and reversible where the agreed list needs "dropped and the teacher is told"; a cancel hides the class where the agreed list needs it greyed and marked Cancelled.

PIPELINE. Three sources end in the same function. (1) File/paste upload: Admin/AdminEndpoints.cs:241-274 (ReadUpload 634-663 -> ScheduleFile.Read -> ScheduleImport.Parse -> PreviewAsync -> ApplyAsync). (2) Classy Sync extension: extension/background.js:96-163 fetches every course of the current semester one per second (fetcher.js:6-63: section number, teacher = first-name cell + last-name cell, then per class a date, time and room), posts to POST /api/sync/timetable (Admin/SyncEndpoints.cs:213-223). (3) Timetable API connection, optionally every morning (Admin/Connections.cs:231-248, 291-316). (2) and (3) go through SyncEndpoints.KeepAsync (126-152), which only stores a PendingSync row (RowsJson). Nothing changes for anyone until an owner/RSA presses Apply: POST /admin/semesters/{id}/sync/apply (SyncEndpoints.cs:243-267) -> ScheduleImport.ApplyAsync + Labs.AlignAsync + UploadLog. So "EduWave later moved or dropped that session" can only ever be noticed at the moment staff apply (or hand-edit), never earlier. KeepAsync refuses a sync when more than max(3, 25%) of courses failed or more than max(5, 25%) of courses would be removed (132, 142); it has no guard at section or session level. Courses EduWave did not answer for are re-emitted from the database so they look unchanged (BuildRows 107-116).

IDENTITY ACROSS A RE-IMPORT (Schedule/ScheduleImport.cs ApplyAsync 328-424).
- Course: matched by Code within the semester, case-insensitive (byCode 347, 384). Codes are stored with all whitespace removed and upper-cased (ScheduleFile.cs:118); EduWave's "CS 1 107" is mapped back to the stored code by SyncEndpoints.Key/BuildRows (29, 83-86). Unique index (SemesterId, Code) (Data/AppDb.cs:123). Course.Id is stable for the life of the semester. A course missing from the upload is deleted (379) unless someone picked it or it has default settings, in which case the course row stays but all its sections are dropped (371-380).
- Section: matched by Number within the course, case-insensitive, after NormalizeSection ("01"/"Sec 1"/"S1" -> "1") (166-174, 398, 402). Unique index (CourseId, Number) (AppDb.cs:134). Section.Id is stable as long as that course code + section number keep appearing. A section missing from the upload goes through DropSection (352-369): picks get SectionId=null + SectionRemoved=true, session notes are detached, the Section row is deleted and its Meetings cascade (AppDb.cs:136). If the same section number reappears in a later sync it is a brand-new row with a new Id (ImportTests.cs:207-230 shows the course keeps its id while its section is re-created).
- Meeting: NO stable identity. If DescribeChange (191-231) finds any difference in a section - one room on one date, or only the instructor string - every Meeting row of that section is deleted and re-inserted (414-418), so all its meeting ids change. Only a section with no difference at all keeps its rows (415 continue). The dashboard section editor does the same (AdminEndpoints.cs:324-344, RemoveRange at 335). Meeting has no key other than its content: SectionId, Day, Start, End, Room, Date (Data/Entities.cs:184-195).
- Instructor: a free-text column on Section (Entities.cs:177), simply overwritten (416). Parse keeps one instructor per section: a second, different name on the same section is discarded with a warning (121-124). Sync clips it to 120 chars (SyncEndpoints.cs:103). DescribeChange compares instructors with Ordinal (case-sensitive) equality (204, 229), so a capitalisation or spacing change counts as a change, reissues all meeting ids and alerts every student in the section with "Instructor: A -> B".

CHANGE STAMPS. Section.ChangedAt / ChangeSummary (Entities.cs:179-181) are one pair per section, overwritten by each later change. They are set only when the semester is the published one (markChanges 348, 419; section editor 340), with a timestamp taken after the write lock is held so the notification worker's watermark works (330-333; AdminEndpoints.cs:337-342). For dated timetables the summary is only "Changes on 12 Oct, 19 Oct and N more" plus an instructor part (196-206) - it does not say what happened to which session. A newly added section gets no stamp (404-412) and a dropped section has none (the pick flag is the signal). Publishing a semester clears every stamp of that semester (AdminEndpoints.cs:68-69). Students/NotificationWorker (Students/Notifications.cs:234-255, 365-392) polls every 30 s for sections with ChangedAt after the saved mark (AppSetting push.changes.since) and pushes "{code} changed" to students who picked that section, are not muted and have a device; tag change-{sectionId}. PushSubscription.StudentId is a required FK to Students (Entities.cs:63-71, AppDb.cs:157-162), so only students can receive pushes today.

THE ONE EXISTING "CHANGE ON TOP OF A UNIVERSITY SESSION" MECHANISM is the batch-rep planner (switched off). It keys a change by PlannerSource(CourseId, SectionId, Fingerprint, Date, Start, End) (Planner/PlannerModels.cs:85) where Fingerprint = SHA-256 of CourseId|SectionId|Day|Start|End|Room|Date (Planner/PlannerEngine.cs:17) - content, not Meeting.Id. After a re-import, an event whose fingerprint no longer exists is "stale": PlannerEngine.PublishedAsync (193-203) silently filters it out of every student view, and Calendar (124-135) shows it flagged for the reps. Because Room is in the fingerprint, a room-only change by the university silently cancels the rep's change and nobody is told (proved by PlannerTests.cs:127-145). Planner Validate also refuses a class change that targets more than one section (PlannerEngine.cs:57). A cancelled/moved occurrence is removed from the student's class via PublishedPlan.For -> Excluded -> MeetingDto.ExcludedDates (PlannerEngine.cs:222-245, Students/StudentEndpoints.cs:329-337, Schedule/Dtos.cs:6) - it disappears; there is no "greyed out, Cancelled" state.

Other code that already identifies one session by natural key: Absence unique (StudentId, CourseId, Date, Start) (AppDb.cs:153), ClassNote (SectionId, Date) (Entities.cs:251-269), reminder tag class-{CourseId}-{date}-{HHmm} and link /?session={courseId}.{date}.{HH:mm} (Notifications.cs:201-202).

NEW SEMESTER. Publish (AdminEndpoints.cs:59-80) only flips IsCurrent, clears stamps and queues "X is out". The new semester has its own Course/Section/Meeting rows (Course.SemesterId), so every id is new; the old semester's rows stay until staff delete the semester (109-117, cascades). Students must redo setup (StudentEndpoints.cs:27-41) and are shown last semester's course codes as suggestions (232-237). Things that are meant to outlive a semester are keyed by text, e.g. MajorElective.CourseCode "so they survive semesters" (Entities.cs:136-145).

A section that returns in the next sync is a new row with a new id.

Sections are matched only by number (ScheduleImport.cs:402). If the university renumbers (section 2 becomes 1), picks, hand-picked sections and teacher changes silently attach to a different real class. Existing behaviour, but teacher changes make the consequence visible to students.

About 12% of teacher time-slots are one lesson listed under 2-3 course codes. A change keyed to one section, as the planner enforces (PlannerEngine.cs:57), would cancel the class for the LOG students and leave it standing for the BE and IBSM students in the same room.

risks: Planner switch is off in production and every overlay today hides behind it: StudentSchedule.ForAsync only applies changes when `planner` is true (StudentSchedule.cs:73), FreeRooms only overlays when PlannerEngine.Enabled (FreeRooms.cs:60). If teacher changes are wired through the planner path they will silently do nothing live.

Two timetable code paths: /me/timetable (StudentEndpoints.cs:312-368) does not use StudentSchedule. If only one is changed, the app shows a class as on while reminders/feed/rooms treat it as cancelled, or the reverse.

Stale device after an identity switch: the endpoint only moves when the subscription is re-posted (push.ts:34-44, called from NotificationsSheet.tsx:24 and Setup.tsx:334), and logout only cleans up for students (AuthEndpoints.cs:319). A teacher signing in at /teach on a browser where a student is still signed in (the cookie is simply replaced, Session.cs:34-41) would keep receiving that student's class reminders on the device - a privacy leak of one person's timetable to another.

iPhone push needs the app on the Home Screen (push.ts:17-18) and the manifest opens it at '/' (manifest.json:5-6). An installed app may not carry over the browser's sign-in, so a teacher can land on the student sign-in screen, which by design has no teacher option - teachers on iPhone might be unable to get reminders at all unless '/' can lead a teacher back to their sign-in.

Reusing Section.ChangedAt for teacher changes would lose alerts and mislabel things: one summary slot per section (Entities.cs:180-181), tag change-{sectionId} collapses different sessions (Notifications.cs:253), publish wipes it (AdminEndpoints.cs:69), a re-sync overwrites it (ScheduleImport.cs:419), and it lights the whole-course 'Changed' badge (StudentEndpoints.cs:362).

'At once' is really up to 30 s (worker tick, Notifications.cs:316) plus delivery, and sends are sequential with a 15 s timeout per device (Program.cs:35; Notifications.cs:270-295). A large section with a slow push service delays the rest of the round, including class reminders, which run in the same loop.

Calendar apps refresh hourly at best (CalendarFeed.cs:170-171) and often slower; a same-day cancellation will usually not reach Apple/Google calendars in time. Students relying only on the calendar feed, students who muted change alerts (Notifications.cs:246) and students not on Classy are not told at once.

Meeting ids are recreated on any section change (ScheduleImport.cs:417-418, AdminEndpoints.cs:335-336): anchoring a teacher change to Meeting.Id loses it on the next re-sync. The .ics UID also embeds MeetingId (CalendarFeed.cs:185), so events already churn after a re-sync; a moved class given a brand-new UID would show as delete + add in calendars.

Planner fingerprint includes room and end time (PlannerEngine.cs:17). If the same key is copied for teacher changes, a room-only edit in EduWave would count as 'EduWave moved it' and drop a teacher's cancellation, re-showing a cancelled class.

Dropped sections cascade: Section deletion removes meetings and (via Pick.SectionId SetNull) unhooks students (AppDb.cs:132-145). A teacher-change table with a cascading FK would vanish with the section before the teacher is told and would erase the dashboard log.

Replaced instructor is not alerted: change-alert recipients are computed from the section as it is when the worker runs (Notifications.cs:241-248). When a re-sync swaps the instructor, the teacher who lost the class no longer matches. New sections under a teacher's name (ScheduleImport.cs:404-412, no ChangedAt) and removed sections (352-369) raise no alert for anyone today.

Clash count can expose one person: with one or two Classy students in a section, 'N have another class then' queried slot by slot reveals an individual's whole timetable, even though only a number is shown (Busy.cs gives per-student blocks). Same for class size on any section a teacher is allowed to add under item 3.

Absence numbers drift: the server lets a session be marked missed any time on its date before it starts (Absences.cs:57) and never removes rows; a class cancelled after that leaves a row counted in the numerator (Session.tsx:141) while the denominator (absences.ts:103-115) drops, pushing a student's percentage up wrongly. If the cancelled class stays in the client session list (as agreed, greyed) and counts()/heldSoFar() are not updated, it also inflates 'of Y' and offers 'I missed this' on a cancelled class.

Rep precedence leak: a rep's published move of the same session adds a replacement event (PlannerEngine.cs:238-241). Skipping only the original for a teacher cancel leaves the rep's replacement in reminders, feed, busy times and free rooms.

Teacher-typed room names only match free rooms if spelled like the timetable (trim + case-insensitive, FreeRooms.cs:69); 'A 101' vs 'A101' would leave the room showing as free while a moved class is in it.

'New semester is out' is sent to every row in PushSubscriptions with a student URL (Notifications.cs:218-219); if teacher devices share that table teachers get 'Set up your courses' and land on /setup.

Calendar token lookup is by table (CalendarFeed.cs:66, 78): a teacher's link keeps serving their teaching timetable to anyone holding it until the token is cleared, so removing a teacher or un-approving a name must reset it.

Delete-all-data test and student-removal test (GroupTests.cs:221-259) assert exact clean-up; new teacher tables with FKs to Section/Semester can make those deletes fail on SQLite FK checks if cascades are missed.

1. Email: trim, lowercase; domain must be exactly gutech.edu.om (student.gutech.edu.om and look-alike hosts refused). For AUTO-link the local part must be letters-only words joined by dots/hyphens/underscores, at least two words, no digits.

3. Normalise each name: strip diacritics, lowercase, drop title words (dr, prof, mr, ms, mrs, eng), split on spaces and hyphens, keep letters only.
4. questions.question: When a teacher adds a course or section that is NOT under their name, what can they do with it?
questions.why: This is the biggest safety decision. Class changes go live at once and notify students. If a self-added section carries the same powers, anyone with a staff email can cancel any class in the university, and the owner/RSA name approval stops protecting anything. But 20 sections (most labs) sit under placeholder names like 'CS1 CS1', so their real teachers can only get them this way.
options: See it only (on their timetable, calendar and reminders). Never change it.
See it at once; cancel/move/room/extra only after an owner or RSA approves that section for them
Full powers at once, no approval
questions.recommended: See it at once; change powers only after an owner or RSA approves that section for them

questions.question: For a section a teacher added themselves and that is NOT yet approved, do they see its class size number and the 'how many students are busy then' count?
questions.why: If yes, any staff member can read enrolment numbers for any class in the university, and on tiny sections learn when one particular student is busy, just by adding the section.
options: No: size and clash count only for sections they are allowed to change
Yes: for every section on their timetable
questions.recommended: No: size and clash count only for sections they are allowed to change

questions.question: Can a teacher who is still waiting for their name to be approved add other courses or sections?
questions.why: A waiting person is unverified. If they can add sections (and those carry any powers or numbers), the waiting state means nothing. It also lets a stranger with any staff address build a watch list of other people's classes.
options: No: adding sections starts only after their name is approved or auto-linked
Yes, but view only
Yes, same as an approved teacher
questions.recommended: No: adding sections starts only after their name is approved or auto-linked

questions.question: Who is allowed to sign in at /teach at all?
questions.why: Every GUtech staff address (registrars, IT, assistants) fits the email rule, not only teachers. If all of them get in and can add sections, the group that could reach class-change powers is the whole staff list instead of about 83 teachers.
options: Any @gutech.edu.om address; people with no timetable name can only view what they add until staff approve them
Only addresses that match a timetable name, plus addresses an owner or RSA has added by hand
Any @gutech.edu.om address with the same rights as a linked teacher
questions.recommended: Any @gutech.edu.om address; people with no timetable name can only view what they add until staff approve them

questions.question: For very small sections (only a few Classy students picked it), should the class size and the 'N students have another class then' count still be shown?
questions.why: The numbers carry no names, but in a section with 1 or 2 Classy students '1 of 1 is busy at 10:00' is that one student's timetable. By trying slot after slot a teacher could map a single student's whole week. Real sections can be this small.
options: Below 5 Classy students show 'fewer than 5' and no clash count
Always show the exact numbers
Show class size always, but hide the clash count below 5
questions.recommended: Below 5 Classy students show 'fewer than 5' and no clash count

questions.question: Should the clash count when moving a class count only students' other classes, or also their private own slots (gym, study, work)?
questions.why: Own slots are private: in groups Classy deliberately shows them only as 'Busy'. Counting them here leaks that a student has something private at that time.
options: Classes only
Classes and own slots
questions.recommended: Classes only

questions.question: When an email auto-links to a name with no human check, should anything extra happen?
questions.why: The email only proves the person owns that address, not that they are the teacher on the timetable. Two staff with the same first and last name (likely with names such as Mohammed Al Balushi), or a non-teaching employee with a teacher's name, would get that teacher's classes and could cancel them at once.
options: Link at once with full powers, and tell owners and RSA each time (shown in the dashboard log, one tap to reverse)
Link at once but the teacher can only view until an owner or RSA taps OK the first time
Link at once, tell nobody
questions.recommended: Link at once with full powers, and tell owners and RSA each time (shown in the dashboard log, one tap to reverse)

questions.question: Can two teacher accounts hold the same timetable name, and what if someone has already picked a name by hand when the real matching email signs in?
questions.why: A person could pick 'Raed Bolbol' first. If that blocks the real raed.bolbol@ from auto-linking, the real teacher is locked out; if both can hold it, two people can cancel the same classes.
options: One account per name. A matching email always wins over a hand pick; staff are alerted to the conflict
One account per name. First come first served; staff sort it out
Several accounts may share a name once staff approve each
questions.recommended: One account per name. A matching email always wins over a hand pick; staff are alerted to the conflict

questions.question: When an owner or RSA removes a teacher, is that email blocked from coming back?
questions.why: Today removing a student is not a ban: they sign in again. A removed teacher whose email matches a name would be auto-linked again the next minute with full cancel powers.
options: Blocked until an owner or RSA unblocks it
Can sign in again but is never auto-linked; needs approval again
Can come back freely
questions.recommended: Blocked until an owner or RSA unblocks it

questions.question: When a teacher is removed (or loses a name), what happens to the cancellations and moves they already made on future classes?
questions.why: If the removal is for misuse, their fake cancellations stay on students' timetables and the teacher can no longer undo them. If the teacher simply left, the cancellations may be real and undoing them would send students to empty rooms.
options: Staff choose at removal: 'also undo their N upcoming changes' (students told the class is back on)
Always undo all of them
Always leave them; staff undo one by one from the log
questions.recommended: Staff choose at removal: 'also undo their N upcoming changes' (students told the class is back on)

questions.question: Should there be a limit on how many class changes one teacher can make in a day?
questions.why: One session at a time does not stop someone tapping Cancel forty times. A stolen or misused sign-in could cancel a whole week for hundreds of students, each with a notification, before anyone looks at the log.
options: Owners and RSA are alerted when a teacher passes 5 changes in a day; hard stop at 20 until staff allow more
Alert staff only, never stop
No limit
questions.recommended: Owners and RSA are alerted when a teacher passes 5 changes in a day; hard stop at 20 until staff allow more

questions.question: Should there be a limit on how many times the same session can be changed and undone?
questions.why: Every cancel, undo and re-cancel sends students a notification. Flipping one class back and forth spams the whole section and leaves students unsure whether the class is on.
options: After 3 changes to the same session, further changes need an owner or RSA
No limit
questions.recommended: After 3 changes to the same session, further changes need an owner or RSA

questions.question: How late can a teacher move a class or add an extra class?
questions.why: A class moved to start in ten minutes, or an extra class added for tonight, reaches students too late and is an easy way to cause chaos. Cancelling late is different: it is often real (the teacher is ill).
options: Cancel any time until the class starts; a move or extra class must be at least 12 hours ahead
Cancel any time; move or extra class at least 2 hours ahead
No minimum notice for anything
questions.recommended: Cancel any time until the class starts; a move or extra class must be at least 12 hours ahead

questions.question: How long should a teacher stay signed in?
questions.why: Students stay signed in for 60 days. A teacher's sign-in can cancel classes, teachers often use shared lecture-room or office computers, and a teacher who leaves GUtech loses their mailbox but keeps a live Classy sign-in. There is also no 'sign out everywhere' for code sign-ins today.
options: 14 days, then a new emailed code
60 days for viewing, but a fresh code is needed before changing a class if the last code was more than 7 days ago
60 days like students
Ends when the browser closes unless they tick 'keep me signed in on this device'
questions.recommended: 60 days for viewing, but a fresh code is needed before changing a class if the last code was more than 7 days ago

questions.question: Should a teacher (and staff, for a teacher) have a 'sign out everywhere' button?
questions.why: If a teacher left a lecture-room PC signed in, or a phone is lost, there is currently no way to end that sign-in short of removing the teacher.
options: Yes: for the teacher in their menu, and for owners/RSA on the Teachers page
No
questions.recommended: Yes: for the teacher in their menu, and for owners/RSA on the Teachers page

questions.question: Should a teacher get an email when their account is signed in on a new device?
questions.why: It is the only way a real teacher finds out that someone else got into their mailbox or account before classes get cancelled in their name.
options: Yes, a short 'new sign-in' email on first use of a device
No
questions.recommended: Yes, a short 'new sign-in' email on first use of a device

questions.question: Should Classy send a sign-in code to any staff address someone types at /teach?
questions.why: Anyone who finds /teach can make Classy email codes to any staff inbox (today's limits allow 20 a day per address and a thousand requests per network every five minutes). That annoys staff, wrongly typed addresses bounce, and it uses the same sending account students' sign-in codes depend on.
options: Any staff address, but much tighter limits (for example 5 a day per address and a low cap per network)
Only addresses that match a timetable name or that staff added; others are told to contact the Classy team
Any staff address with the same limits students have
questions.recommended: Any staff address, but much tighter limits (for example 5 a day per address and a low cap per network)

questions.question: Should launch wait until a real staff mailbox has received a Classy sign-in code?
questions.why: Teacher codes can never be shown on screen (that would let anyone become any teacher), so email is the only way in. Delivery has only been proven for student mailboxes. If the staff mail system filters it, no teacher can sign in on launch day.
options: Yes: test with one or two real staff addresses first
No: launch and fix if it fails
questions.recommended: Yes: test with one or two real staff addresses first

questions.question: Do you want an owner switch that turns off all teacher class changes at once, and a 'freeze' for a single teacher?
questions.why: Everything ships at once to everyone with no trial. If something is being misused or is broken, the only tools today would be removing teachers one by one or a new deploy.
options: Both: one switch for all teacher changes, and freeze one teacher (they can still view)
Only the switch for everyone
Neither
questions.recommended: Both: one switch for all teacher changes, and freeze one teacher (they can still view)

questions.question: When an owner or RSA undoes a teacher's change, can the teacher simply make the same change again?
questions.why: If yes, a staff undo of a wrong or abusive cancellation can be overridden straight away, and students get a third notification.
options: No: that session is locked for the teacher after a staff undo
Yes
questions.recommended: No: that session is locked for the teacher after a staff undo

questions.question: When staff undo a teacher's change: is the teacher told, are students notified again, and must staff give a reason?
questions.why: Without telling the teacher they may turn up to (or skip) the wrong session; without a reason the teacher does not know why. Students always need the 'class is back on' message.
options: Teacher and students are told; a short reason is optional
Teacher and students are told; a reason is required and shown to the teacher
Only students are told
questions.recommended: Teacher and students are told; a short reason is optional

questions.question: Should students see who made a change (for example 'Cancelled by Raed Bolbol')?
questions.why: With added sections, the person cancelling may not be the lecturer students know. Showing the name lets students and the listed teacher spot a change that looks wrong; hiding it makes a wrongful cancellation look official.
options: Yes, always show the name of the teacher who made the change
Only when it is not the listed lecturer
No
questions.recommended: Yes, always show the name of the teacher who made the change

questions.question: Should a cancelled or moved class have a 'This looks wrong' button for students that goes to owners and RSA?
questions.why: Changes are live with no approval, so students are the first to notice a fake or mistaken cancellation. Today 'Report a problem' is buried in the menu.
options: Yes, reuse the existing problem report from the class page
No
questions.recommended: Yes, reuse the existing problem report from the class page

questions.question: When someone else adds a section that is under a teacher's name, or changes one of its classes, is the listed teacher told?
questions.why: Otherwise the listed teacher can find their class cancelled by a colleague (or by a stranger with a staff address) with no warning.
options: Yes: told when someone is approved for their section and on every change by the other person
Only on changes
No
questions.recommended: Yes: told when someone is approved for their section and on every change by the other person

questions.question: When two teachers can change the same section, who may undo a change?
questions.why: If only the person who made it can undo, the listed teacher cannot fix a colleague's mistake. If either can, they can keep overriding each other.
options: Either teacher with change rights on the section, and the other is told
Only the one who made it, plus owners and RSA
questions.recommended: Either teacher with change rights on the section, and the other is told

questions.question: Does a teacher who added a section show to students as teaching it (name on the class page, office hours, listed on their teacher page)?
questions.why: If self-adding is enough, anyone with a staff address can present themselves to students as the teacher of any class.
options: Only after an owner or RSA approved that section for them
As soon as they add it
Never: students only see the EduWave name
questions.recommended: Only after an owner or RSA approved that section for them

questions.question: Which email address can a teacher choose to show to students?
questions.why: If the field is free text, a wrongly linked or malicious account could show any address and collect students' emails. The agreed list only says email is off unless turned on.
options: Only the staff address they signed in with (a simple on/off)
Any address they type
questions.recommended: Only the staff address they signed in with (a simple on/off)

questions.question: Who can open a teacher's page (office hours, room, note, optional email)?
questions.why: It holds a staff member's whereabouts and possibly their email. The public timetable link, if switched on, is open to anyone on the internet.
options: Any signed-in Classy student or teacher; never on the public timetable link
Only students who have one of that teacher's classes
questions.recommended: Any signed-in Classy student or teacher; never on the public timetable link

questions.question: What limits apply to the free text a teacher writes (note to students, office note, typed room)?
questions.why: This text is pushed to students' lock screens and shown on every class page with no review. It could carry links, abuse or personal data.
options: Plain text, about 140 characters, links not clickable; owners and RSA can remove it from the log
Longer text with links allowed
questions.recommended: Plain text, about 140 characters, links not clickable; owners and RSA can remove it from the log

questions.question: Is it fine for RSA to see teachers' staff email addresses and the full log of which teacher changed what?
questions.why: The written rule only says RSA sees no student data; it says nothing about staff. RSA need the email to judge a picked name, but it is personal data about colleagues.
options: Yes: RSA see teacher name, staff email and the change log; never student names or IDs
RSA see names only; emails are owner-only
questions.recommended: Yes: RSA see teacher name, staff email and the change log; never student names or IDs

questions.question: Should owners be told whenever an RSA approves a name, attaches a name or approves an added section?
questions.why: An RSA account can create other RSA accounts today, so any RSA can make a new approver. One careless or dishonest approval gives a person the power to cancel real classes.
options: Yes: every approval is logged with who did it and owners get a notice on the dashboard home
Logged only
No
questions.recommended: Yes: every approval is logged with who did it and owners get a notice on the dashboard home

questions.question: You have no staff address, so you cannot sign in as a teacher. Do you want owners to be able to open the teacher view for any name from the dashboard?
questions.why: It helps support and testing, but with the change buttons it is a way to cancel classes in a teacher's name.
options: Yes, view only
Yes, with change buttons; changes are logged as made by the owner
No
questions.recommended: Yes, view only

questions.question: When the university timetable gives a section to a different teacher, what happens to the first teacher's upcoming cancellations and moves, and does the new name's teacher get change powers automatically?
questions.why: Powers follow the name text. EduWave or an RSA retyping the instructor hands cancel rights to whoever holds the new name with no approval, and the old teacher's changes are left with nobody who can undo them except staff. This already happened once this month (ENG4135 section 2).
options: Old changes stay; the new teacher and staff can undo them; both teachers and staff are told
Old changes are dropped; students are told the class is back on; both teachers are told
Old changes stay and nobody is told
questions.recommended: Old changes stay; the new teacher and staff can undo them; both teachers and staff are told

questions.question: If a linked name is re-spelled in the timetable, should Classy follow it automatically?
questions.why: Following automatically could hand one person's classes to another (Ahmad/Ahmed, Mohamed/Mohammed, Yousuf/Yusuf are different people in the real data). Not following empties the teacher's timetable until staff act.
options: Never automatic: staff get a 'probably the same person' prompt and confirm with one tap
Follow automatically when the same sections simply carry a new spelling
questions.recommended: Never automatic: staff get a 'probably the same person' prompt and confirm with one tap

questions.question: How many extra courses or sections may one teacher add, and how many names may a person try to claim?
questions.why: Without a cap one account can add all 306 sections (to watch everything and flood staff with approval requests) or keep claiming names after each rejection.
options: Up to 10 added sections; one waiting name at a time; blocked after 3 rejections until staff unblock
No limits
questions.recommended: Up to 10 added sections; one waiting name at a time; blocked after 3 rejections until staff unblock

questions.question: While waiting for approval, what exactly can a teacher open?
questions.why: The list says 'only view the timetable for the name they picked', but the free rooms page is open to anyone signed in today. An unverified person should not get the calendar link, reminders, class sizes, or a public teacher page.
options: Only that name's timetable: no free rooms, calendar link, reminders, class size, office hours or teacher page
Timetable plus free rooms
questions.recommended: Only that name's timetable: no free rooms, calendar link, reminders, class size, office hours or teacher page

questions.question: If a teacher opens /teach on a browser where a student (or dashboard account) is still signed in, what happens?
questions.why: A browser holds one sign-in. Silently replacing it leaves the previous person's notifications tied to that device and their saved timetable on it, so one person can receive or see the other's timetable.
options: Classy signs the other person out properly first (their notifications and saved timetable are removed from the device)
Just replace the sign-in
questions.recommended: Classy signs the other person out properly first (their notifications and saved timetable are removed from the device)

questions.question: May a device remember that a teacher used it, so the app opens the teacher sign-in instead of the student one after sign-out?
questions.why: Without it a teacher who installed the app lands on the student ID screen with no way back (iPhone notifications need the installed app). With it, the next student on a shared computer sees the teacher sign-in, which students are not supposed to see.
options: Yes on that device only, with a small 'I'm a student' link back
No: teachers always type /teach
questions.recommended: Yes on that device only, with a small 'I'm a student' link back

questions.question: The student sign-in screen says 'Staff? Sign in here' and leads to the dashboard password login. Teachers are staff and will tap it. Change it?
questions.why: Teachers typing their email and guessing passwords on the dashboard login adds failed logins against real dashboard accounts, and it conflicts with the rule that students see no teacher option.
options: Reword to 'Classy team? Sign in here' and leave no teacher hint
Keep the wording; add a line on the dashboard login pointing teachers to /teach
Leave as is
questions.recommended: Reword to 'Classy team? Sign in here' and leave no teacher hint

questions.question: Should 'Delete all data' also delete teacher accounts, and the list of blocked emails?
questions.why: If teacher rows are forgotten, staff emails and office details survive a wipe that claims to delete everything; if the block list is wiped, removed people can return.
options: Delete teachers' changes, added sections and office hours; keep teacher accounts, name links and the block list (like dashboard accounts)
Delete everything about teachers
Keep everything about teachers
questions.recommended: Delete teachers' changes, added sections and office hours; keep teacher accounts, name links and the block list (like dashboard accounts)

questions.question: How long is the log of teacher changes kept, and does it stay after a new semester is published?
questions.why: The log is the only record of who cancelled what. If it dies with the semester or with a dropped section, a complaint about a past cancellation cannot be checked.
options: Kept for good, readable even after the section or semester is gone
Kept for the current semester only
questions.recommended: Kept for good, readable even after the section or semester is gone

questions.question: Should teachers see anything about attendance (how many students marked a class missed)?
questions.why: The list covers notes and class size but not absences. Absence marks are a student's private record; even a count on a small section points at individuals.
options: No attendance information at all
A count only
questions.recommended: No attendance information at all

questions.question: Do name links need to be confirmed again each semester?
questions.why: A teacher who left GUtech keeps a linked account. If the university re-uses the name or the person keeps a signed-in device, powers continue with nobody checking.
options: Links carry over, but owners and RSA get a list at each new semester of linked teachers who have not signed in recently, with one-tap remove
Every link must be re-approved each semester
Links carry over with no review
questions.recommended: Links carry over, but owners and RSA get a list at each new semester of linked teachers who have not signed in recently, with one-tap remove

contradictions: Item 3 (a teacher can pick other courses or sections) plus item 5 (changes are live at once, no approval) cancels out item 2 (a name needs a clear email match or owner/RSA approval). Unless picked sections are view-only or separately approved, any staff email holder can cancel any class in the university.

Item 2 says a waiting teacher 'can only view the timetable for the name they picked', but the free rooms endpoint is open to any signed-in account (SignedInPolicy, C:\Projects\Scheduele\server\UniSchedule.Api\Program.cs:66; FreeRooms.cs:93) and item 4 lists free rooms, calendar feed and reminders as teacher extras. Waiting teachers get them unless each is explicitly gated on an approved link.

Item 8 says 'a number only, no names or IDs' as if that protects students, but class size is the count of Classy picks, which is often 1-3. A clash count of '1 of 1' is one student's timetable, and the busy data it would be built on includes private own slots that groups deliberately show only as 'Busy'.

Item 11 lets RSA approve and attach names, while any RSA can create further RSA accounts (C:\Projects\Scheduele\server\UniSchedule.Api\Admin\OwnerEndpoints.cs:85-99: only creating an owner is owner-only). The human check on who may cancel classes is therefore only as strong as the least careful RSA account.

Item 11 'remove a teacher' does not hold with item 2's auto-link: sign-in creates the account on first verify, so a removed teacher whose email matches a name is linked again on their next sign-in unless a block is stored.

Item 5 gives the teacher undo 'until the class starts' and item 11 lets staff remove a teacher; after removal the teacher's live cancellations stay on students' timetables with no one but staff able to undo them, and nothing says whether staff can undo after the start.

Item 1 says students never see a teacher option, but the student sign-in already shows 'Staff? Sign in here' (web/src/student/Login.tsx:243-248) leading to the dashboard login, and the only fix for teachers landing on the student screen after sign-out (remembering the device) shows the teacher sign-in to the next student on a shared computer.

Item 12 'live straight away for everyone' depends on email codes reaching staff mailboxes, which has never been tested; and teacher codes must never be shown on screen, while the existing test mode shows codes for everyone who is not an owner or batch rep (AuthEndpoints.cs:158-163). If the teacher path copies the student one, a test-mode server lets anyone become any teacher.

Item 6 says a teacher's change is dropped when EduWave moves or drops the session. The existing overlay key (planner fingerprint) includes the room, and 16 of 18 real session changes between two exports were room-only. Reused as-is, a room-only university change would drop a teacher's cancellation and show the class as on again after students were told it was cancelled, and the existing mechanism drops silently where item 6 says the teacher is told.

Item 6 assumes Classy notices when EduWave changes a session, but a sync changes nothing until an owner or RSA presses Apply (which can be hours later). A teacher can make a change in between, and staff apply a sync without seeing which teacher changes it will drop.

Item 5 says a cancelled class stays greyed out and marked Cancelled; today every cancel path hides the class (excludedDates, web/src/lib/slots.ts:177-182). If the greyed block is fed through the normal session list it will also be counted as live, as a clash, in attendance totals and in reminders.

Item 7 says students are told at once. The notification worker runs every 30 seconds, the existing change stamp is one slot and one notification tag per section (a second change replaces the first), students who muted change alerts or keep the app open get nothing until a reload, and calendar feeds lag by hours.

Item 10 says a teacher's change always wins over a batch rep's, but the planner's one-change-per-session rule only knows planner events, and the planner is switched off in production, so the 'teacher wins' code would ship with no real use and no test unless written.

Students stay signed in 60 days with a sliding cookie and there is no 'sign out everywhere' for code sign-ins (only dashboard accounts have a session version). Giving the same sign-in the power to cancel classes on shared lecture-room PCs contradicts how carefully the dashboard login is protected.

The timetable name is treated as proof of who teaches a class, but the real data lists the same name in two rooms at the same time on 64 slots, 32 room slots under two names at once, and 20 sections under placeholder accounts. An auto-linked teacher therefore gets live powers over some classes they do not teach, while the real teacher of a placeholder lab has none.

risks.risk: Any staff email holder cancels any class: self-picked sections combined with instant, unapproved changes and immediate student notifications.
risks.mitigation: Change powers only on sections under an approved/auto-linked name or sections an owner or RSA approved for that teacher. Enforce on the server per section on every change request, not in the picker UI. Add a test that a teacher gets 403 changing a section they merely added.

risks.risk: An unapproved (waiting) teacher reaches a write endpoint because one route was put on the general teacher policy instead of the linked-teacher policy.
risks.mitigation: Two policies with new role strings ('teacher', 'teacher-pending'); every endpoint that writes, notifies students, or returns size/clash numbers requires 'teacher'. One test walks every /api/teach route as a pending teacher and expects 403 on all but the view-only ones.

risks.risk: Wrong-person auto-link: same first and last name, a non-teaching employee with a teacher's name, or a numbered/alias address gets a teacher's classes instantly.
risks.mitigation: Exact matching only (no fuzzy or sounds-like), no digits, exactly one match, name not already linked or claimed. Log every auto-link, notify owners/RSA, one-tap reverse. Re-run the collision check against the live export before release.

risks.risk: Test mode shows a teacher's code on screen, so anyone typing a lecturer's address becomes that lecturer.
risks.mitigation: The teacher request-code endpoint never returns testCode, whatever the setting. Tests read the code from a capturing email sender. Add a test asserting testCode is null for a staff address with test mode on.

risks.risk: Identity mix-up between tables: the cookie holds a bare row number, and every /api/me handler reads Students by that number. If a teacher ever passes the student policy, teacher 7 reads and writes student 7's picks, notes and absences; the /auth/session fall-through would show a teacher as the dashboard account with the same number.
risks.mitigation: Teachers are a separate table and kind with their own /api/teach group; StudentPolicy stays kind == student exactly; /auth/session and ActorName get explicit kind branches. Test that a signed-in teacher gets 403 on every /api/me and /api/admin route.

risks.risk: Removed teacher returns: sign-in creates the account on first verify and the email re-auto-links.
risks.mitigation: Store a block on the email at removal; verify refuses blocked addresses with the same neutral message. Removal also clears their devices, calendar link and (by staff choice) undoes future changes.

risks.risk: Mass cancelling or notification spam from a misused or stolen teacher sign-in (dozens of single cancels, or cancel/undo loops on one session).
risks.mitigation: Per-teacher daily change limit with a staff alert, per-session change limit, a session locked after a staff undo, an owner kill switch for all teacher changes and a per-teacher freeze. Notification tag per session so later states replace earlier ones.

risks.risk: Stale or shared-device sign-in: a 60-day sign-in on a lecture-room PC, or a teacher who left GUtech and lost their mailbox but keeps a live session, can still cancel classes.
risks.mitigation: Shorter teacher session or a fresh code before any change when the last code is older than a week; 'sign out everywhere' (a session version on the teacher row); email on new-device sign-in; start-of-semester review list of inactive linked teachers.

risks.risk: Shared-device data leak: the saved offline timetable has no owner stamp and is only cleared by a proper logout, and a device's push subscription stays with the previous person until re-posted. A student could see a teacher's saved timetable or receive their alerts, and the reverse.
risks.mitigation: Stamp the saved copy with kind + identity and refuse it for anyone else; clear caches whenever the signed-in identity changes; /teach signs the previous session out through logout first; logout drops the device for teachers too; saving an endpoint for one kind deletes it from the other kind's table in the same transaction.

risks.risk: Small-section privacy: class size and the clash count identify individual students, and repeated move previews map a student's week; own slots would leak private commitments.
risks.mitigation: Minimum threshold (for example 5) below which only 'fewer than 5' is shown and no clash count; classes only, never own slots; no size or clash numbers for sections the teacher cannot change; rate-limit the move-preview endpoint; teacher endpoints never return picks, notes, absences, names or IDs (assert in tests).

risks.risk: Mail abuse through /teach: Classy can be made to email codes to any staff inbox (20 a day per address, up to 1000 requests per 5 minutes per network today), bounces damage the sending reputation student sign-in relies on, and a stranger can use up a teacher's daily allowance to lock them out of a new device.
risks.mitigation: Separate, much lower per-network and per-address limits for the teacher request-code endpoint; strict address validation (exact domain gutech.edu.om, never student.gutech.edu.om, no commas or newlines); identical answer for known and unknown addresses; keep the trusted-device exemption so the real teacher's own devices still work.

risks.risk: Code guessing on the new sign-in path if it is built as a copy that misses one of the existing protections (5 tries per code claimed atomically, browser binding, 30 wrong per day per key, per-network wrong-code cap).
risks.mitigation: Do not copy: move the request-code and verify bodies into shared helpers keyed by a string (student ID or staff email) and call them from both paths, mounted under /api/auth so the binding cookies apply. Port the sign-in safety tests to the email key.

risks.risk: Powers follow free text: EduWave or an RSA retyping Section.Instructor moves cancel rights to whoever holds the new name with no approval; a re-spelling silently empties a teacher's timetable; look-alike names are different people.
risks.mitigation: One shared name-normalising function; never re-link automatically; record old and new instructor at apply time, tell both teachers and staff; staff confirm probable re-spellings with one tap; log instructor edits made in the dashboard.

risks.risk: A re-sync or staff edit silently destroys or revives teacher changes: meeting rows are recreated on any section change, the planner key includes the room, dropped sections cascade-delete dependants, and a section that returns gets a new id. A cancelled class could show as on again with nobody told, or the audit log could lose rows.
risks.mitigation: Key changes on section + date + start (never Meeting.Id, never the room); reconcile inside the apply transaction and in the dashboard section editor; persist the drop with a reason and tell the teacher; keep course code and section number text copies with a nullable section link so the log survives; show 'N teacher changes will be dropped' in the sync/upload preview.

risks.risk: Two timetable code paths (GET /me/timetable and StudentSchedule.ForAsync) and the planner switch being off in production: a teacher cancel could show as Cancelled in the app while reminders, calendar feed, free rooms or group free time still treat the class as on, or do nothing at all live.
risks.mitigation: Apply the teacher overlay in one shared loader used by both paths and never behind the planner switch; tests assert timetable, reminders, feed, free rooms, groups and absence marking all agree with the planner off.

risks.risk: Audit gaps: actor helper assumes 'not a student means dashboard account' (OwnerEndpoints.cs:37-43), so a teacher's action could be logged under the dashboard username with the same row number or throw; approvals by RSA accounts created by other RSA accounts leave no trail to an owner.
risks.mitigation: Make the actor helper kind-aware before any teacher path can call it; append-only log for sign-ins on new devices, auto-links, approvals, attachments, removals, every change, undo and drop, each with who and when; owners see RSA approvals on the dashboard home.

risks.risk: RSA privacy rule broken by the new pages: a change-log row or teacher list that embeds student payloads would show RSA student IDs, and staff emails become visible to RSA with no written rule.
risks.mitigation: Teacher admin endpoints return counts only and pass every 'by' value through the existing ShownActor; test that no RSA teacher payload contains a student ID; write the staff-data rule into docs/plan.md.

risks.risk: Free text from teachers (note, typed room, office note, shown email) is pushed to students unreviewed and could carry links, abuse or a fake contact address.
risks.mitigation: Short length caps, plain text only, shown email limited to the sign-in address, staff can clear a note from the log, students can report a change from the class page.

risks.risk: All-at-once release to real students with about four teaching weeks left: every push to main deploys, rollback only triggers on a failed health check, and restoring the backup later would discard what students did after the deploy.
risks.mitigation: Additive migration only (separate teacher tables, no rebuild of PushSubscriptions); nothing teacher-related reaches main until complete; owner kill switch shipped in the same release, defaulting to on only after the staff-mailbox test passes.

questions.question: When a teacher adds a section that is not under their name, what can they do with it?
questions.why: This is the new request and it decides the whole build. Class changes go live with no approval, so if an added section carries the same powers, any staff email could cancel any class in the university and students would be notified at once. If it is view-only, lab assistants who really teach the 20 sections listed under names like 'CS1 CS1' could never cancel their own lab.
options: See it only: on their timetable, reminders and calendar. Never cancel or move it.
See it at once; cancel/move/room/extra class only after an owner or RSA approves that section (like a name).
Full powers at once for any section they add.
Full powers at once only for sections with no real teacher listed ('CS1 CS1' etc.); sections under another teacher's name need approval.
questions.recommended: See it at once; cancel/move/room/extra class only after an owner or RSA approves that section (like a name).

questions.question: A staff member opens the name picker and their name is not on the list at all (lab assistant, new teacher, the real person behind 'CS1 CS1', or staff who teach nothing). What happens?
questions.why: The agreed list only covers 'pick your name and wait'. Without an answer this person is stuck on a list with nothing to tap. It also decides whether adding sections is a side feature or the only way in for these people.
options: A 'My name is not here' button: they go in with an empty timetable and build it by adding sections (changes still need approval per section).
They are told Classy is for staff on the timetable and asked to contact the Classy team; no account use until an owner attaches a name.
They can only use the free rooms page and view sections; no adding.
questions.recommended: A 'My name is not here' button: they go in with an empty timetable and build it by adding sections (changes still need approval per section).

questions.question: Can a teacher who is still waiting for their name to be approved add other courses or sections?
questions.why: The agreed list says a waiting teacher can only view the timetable for the name they picked. Letting them add sections widens that; not letting them means the add screen must be hidden and explained while they wait.
options: No. Adding sections opens only after the name is approved (or after tapping 'My name is not here').
Yes, but only to look at them; nothing else until approved.
questions.recommended: Yes, but only to look at them; nothing else until approved.

questions.question: You wrote 'courses or sections'. When a teacher picks a course, what lands on their timetable?
questions.why: 26 of 91 teachers teach several sections of one course and many courses have sections under different teachers. 'Whole course' could put ten parallel sections on one timetable and, if the university adds a section later, change it silently.
options: They always tick sections one by one; the course is only the way to find them (with an 'all sections' shortcut).
Picking a course adds every section it has today; later sections are not added.
Picking a course adds every section, including ones the university adds later.
questions.recommended: They always tick sections one by one; the course is only the way to find them (with an 'all sections' shortcut).

questions.question: Do students see a teacher who added their section?
questions.why: Students currently see only the name from EduWave. If an added teacher cancels the class, students get a cancellation from someone not listed on the class. And for 'CS1 CS1' labs, the added teacher is the only real name there is.
options: No. Adding is private to the teacher; students keep seeing only the EduWave name.

Yes, once that section is approved: the class page shows them too ('Also teaching: ...') with their office hours, and the section is listed on their teacher page. A placeholder name is replaced by them.
Yes, as soon as they add it, approved or not.
questions.recommended: Yes, once that section is approved: the class page shows them too ('Also teaching: ...') with their office hours, and the section is listed on their teacher page. A placeholder name is replaced by them.

questions.question: When a teacher adds a section that is under another teacher's name, is the listed teacher told?
questions.why: Two people can then change the same class. The listed teacher would otherwise first find out when their class is cancelled by someone else.
options: Not told.
Told when an owner or RSA approves the other teacher for that section.
Told only when the other teacher actually cancels or moves a class.
questions.recommended: Told when an owner or RSA approves the other teacher for that section.

questions.question: When two teachers are on the same section (one listed, one added), who can undo or replace a change one of them made?
questions.why: If only the author can undo, a wrong cancellation waits for that one person or for staff. If either can, they can flip a class on and off for students.
options: Either teacher on the section, and the other is notified.
Only the teacher who made it, plus owners and RSA.
questions.recommended: Either teacher on the section, and the other is notified.

questions.question: Can a teacher remove a section that EduWave wrongly lists under their name, and what does that do?
questions.why: In the real data one name is listed in two rooms at the same time on 64 slots, so the listed person is not always the one teaching. Without a remove button the teacher's timetable shows clashes and they get reminders for classes that are not theirs; students keep seeing their office hours on a class they do not teach.
options: Yes: 'Not my class' hides it from their timetable, reminders and teacher page, stops showing their details on that class, removes their power to change it, and flags it to staff in the dashboard. They can add it back.
Yes, but it only hides it on their own timetable; students and staff see no difference.
No. They must ask an owner or RSA to fix it.
questions.recommended: Yes: 'Not my class' hides it from their timetable, reminders and teacher page, stops showing their details on that class, removes their power to change it, and flags it to staff in the dashboard. They can add it back.

questions.question: When a new semester is published, what happens to the sections a teacher added themselves?
questions.why: A new semester has all-new sections. Name links carry over by spelling, but added sections cannot be matched safely. The teacher's first screen in the new semester depends on this.
options: Start empty; last semester's added courses are offered as suggestions to tick again.
Carried over automatically wherever the same course code and section number exist.
Start empty with no suggestions.
questions.recommended: Start empty; last semester's added courses are offered as suggestions to tick again.

questions.question: Should owners and RSA see which extra sections each teacher added, approve or remove them, and add one for a teacher from the dashboard?
questions.why: If added sections need approval there must be a place to do it. If they do not, staff still need to see who gave themselves which class.
options: Yes: the Teachers page lists added sections per teacher with Approve, Remove and 'Add a section for this teacher'.
Show the list and Remove only.
Not shown in the dashboard.
questions.recommended: Yes: the Teachers page lists added sections per teacher with Approve, Remove and 'Add a section for this teacher'.

questions.question: For a section a teacher has added but is not approved to change, do they see the class size number?
questions.why: Otherwise any staff email can read how many students are in any class in the university.
options: No number until approved for that section.
Yes, the number shows for anything on their timetable.
questions.recommended: No number until approved for that section.

questions.question: Many lectures are one real class listed under two or three course codes (for example BE1101, IBSM1101 and LOG1101 together in one room; 67 of 306 sections). How should the teacher see and change these?
questions.why: If each code is separate, cancelling one leaves the other two groups of students seeing the class as on, the teacher's own timetable shows three stacked blocks marked as a clash, the 'room is taken' warning reports the teacher's own class, and the class size is a third of the real room.
options: One block on the teacher's timetable; cancel/move/room change applies to all the codes in one tap; class size and clash count are the combined total.
One block, but the teacher can untick a code before confirming.
Separate blocks, changed one by one.
questions.recommended: One block on the teacher's timetable; cancel/move/room change applies to all the codes in one tap; class size and clash count are the combined total.

questions.question: The university later changes only the ROOM of a class the teacher already cancelled or moved (same day and time). Does the teacher's change stay?
questions.why: Room-only changes are the commonest university change (16 of 18 between two real exports). If they drop the teacher's change, a class students were told is cancelled shows as on again and students turn up.
options: It stays. Only a new day or time, or the class disappearing, drops the teacher's change.
It is dropped like any other university change and the teacher is told.
questions.recommended: It stays. Only a new day or time, or the class disappearing, drops the teacher's change.
