questions.question: The teacher changed the room and the university later lists a different room for that same class. Which room do students see?
questions.why: Two sources disagree about where the class is; students walk to one of them.
options: The teacher's room, until the teacher undoes it; the teacher is told the university room changed.
The university's newer room; the teacher's room change is dropped and the teacher is told.
questions.recommended: The teacher's room, until the teacher undoes it; the teacher is told the university room changed.

questions.question: If the university timetable later shows exactly what the teacher did (the class is now officially at the new time), what does the teacher see?
questions.why: Otherwise a teacher who did the right thing gets a 'your change was dropped' message and students get a second 'changed' notification for something they already know.
options: The change quietly merges; no message to the teacher, no second notification to students.
The teacher is told 'now in the university timetable'; students are not notified again.
Treat it as dropped, with the usual messages.
questions.recommended: The change quietly merges; no message to the teacher, no second notification to students.

questions.question: The university gives a section to a different teacher mid-semester. What happens to the first teacher's upcoming cancellations and moves on it?
questions.why: It happened to ENG4135 section 2 this month. If changes stay with nobody able to undo them, students are stuck with a cancellation the new teacher does not know about; if they are dropped silently, a cancelled class comes back.
options: Kept; the new teacher (and staff) can undo them; both teachers are told.
Dropped; students are told the class is back on; both teachers are told.
Kept; only owners and RSA can undo them.
questions.recommended: Kept; the new teacher (and staff) can undo them; both teachers are told.

questions.question: A teacher's name disappears from the timetable after a sync (re-spelled by EduWave, or they have no classes left). What do they see next time they open Classy?
questions.why: Linking is by the spelling of the name. A re-spelling would silently empty a teacher's timetable, and the agreed list does not say whether they are sent back to 'pick your name'.
options: They keep their account, office hours and added sections; the home says 'No classes under your name right now'; staff get a row in the dashboard with a one-tap re-link if a new spelling appeared on the same sections.
Classy follows a re-spelling automatically when the same sections simply carry a new name.
They are sent back to the name picker and wait for approval again.
questions.recommended: They keep their account, office hours and added sections; the home says 'No classes under your name right now'; staff get a row in the dashboard with a one-tap re-link if a new spelling appeared on the same sections.

questions.question: When a class is moved, what do students see at the OLD time?
questions.why: The agreed list says a cancelled class stays greyed out, and that moved classes get a 'Moved' mark, but not whether the old slot stays. A student glancing at Monday needs to know why the usual class is missing.
options: The old slot stays, greyed, saying 'Moved to Tue 10:00'; the class also shows at the new time with a 'Moved' mark.
The class only shows at the new time with a 'Moved' mark; the old slot is empty.
questions.recommended: The old slot stays, greyed, saying 'Moved to Tue 10:00'; the class also shows at the new time with a 'Moved' mark.

questions.question: What times can a teacher pick when moving a class or adding an extra one?
questions.why: The week view is drawn on six fixed class slots (08:00, 09:45, 11:30, 13:15, 15:00, 16:45). A class at an odd time is drawn in the nearest row and can sit on top of another class, so students would see a misleading week.
options: The six class slots as quick buttons, plus any other time; a warning outside 08:00-18:15.
Only the six standard class slots.
Any time at all, no warning.
questions.recommended: The six class slots as quick buttons, plus any other time; a warning outside 08:00-18:15.

questions.question: Which dates can a class be moved to or an extra class added on?
questions.why: The agreed rule is 'warn, never block' for clashes and rooms, but nothing is said about holidays, weekends, dates after the last teaching week, or dates far ahead. A class moved onto a holiday would show as happening.
options: Any future date up to the end of the semester; holidays, Fridays/Saturdays and non-teaching weeks only show a warning.
Only teaching days inside the teaching weeks; holidays and weekends are refused.
Any future date with no warning.
questions.recommended: Any future date up to the end of the semester; holidays, Fridays/Saturdays and non-teaching weeks only show a warning.

questions.question: 'Undo until the class starts': for a moved class, which start time is the cut-off?
questions.why: A Monday class moved to Wednesday: undoing on Tuesday would put the class back in the past, so students lose it entirely. A class moved earlier has the opposite problem.
options: Whichever comes first, the old time or the new time. After that the teacher can still move or cancel the new session, but not undo.
The new time.
The old time.
questions.recommended: Whichever comes first, the old time or the new time. After that the teacher can still move or cancel the new session, but not undo.

questions.question: Can a teacher change a change (move it again, fix the room or the note) without undoing it first?
questions.why: Without it, fixing a typo in the room means undo then redo, and students get 'back on' followed by 'moved' again.
options: Yes. Editing replaces the earlier change and students get one notification with the new details.
No. Undo first, then make a new change.
questions.recommended: Yes. Editing replaces the earlier change and students get one notification with the new details.

questions.question: Very late changes: a teacher undoes a cancellation, or moves a class to a time that starts within the hour. Should Classy do anything?
questions.why: Cancelling 10 minutes before class is covered. But un-cancelling 10 minutes before means students who already left are marked as having a class, and a class moved to 'in 20 minutes' reaches few of them.
options: Allow it, with a warning: 'This starts in 10 minutes; students may not see it in time.'
Refuse undoing a cancellation, or moving a class to a start time, less than one hour away.
Allow it with no warning.
questions.recommended: Allow it, with a warning: 'This starts in 10 minutes; students may not see it in time.'

questions.question: When a teacher undoes a change, are students notified again?
questions.why: Students were told 'cancelled'. If the undo is silent, those who planned around it miss the class.
options: Yes: 'CS1107 Mon 10:00 is back on' to the same students.
No; only the mark on the timetable goes away.
questions.recommended: Yes: 'CS1107 Mon 10:00 is back on' to the same students.

questions.question: When an owner or RSA undoes a teacher's change from the dashboard, what happens around it?
questions.why: The agreed list says staff can undo one, but not whether the teacher hears about it, whether a reason is needed, or whether staff can undo after the class has started.
options: Teacher and students are notified; staff may type a short reason the teacher sees; only future classes can be undone.
Teacher and students are notified; a reason is required.
Students are notified; the teacher just sees it gone.
questions.recommended: Teacher and students are notified; staff may type a short reason the teacher sees; only future classes can be undone.

questions.question: Do students see who made the change?
questions.why: With added teachers and staff undo, a cancellation may come from someone not listed on the class. A notification with no name can look like a mistake or a prank.
options: Yes, the teacher's name: 'Cancelled by Raed Bolbol', plus the note.
Only 'Cancelled by your lecturer'.
No name at all.
questions.recommended: Yes, the teacher's name: 'Cancelled by Raed Bolbol', plus the note.

questions.question: RSA edits a section by hand in the dashboard and one of its sessions already has a teacher's cancel or move. What happens?
questions.why: The dashboard editor shows the university time for every session and saves the whole list. Today RSA would not even see that a teacher cancelled it, and a save could wipe the teacher's change or leave both in force.
options: The editor marks sessions that carry a teacher's change and warns on save; the same rule as EduWave then applies (room-only edit keeps the teacher's change, a new day/time drops it and the teacher is told).
RSA must undo the teacher's change first before editing that session.
The teacher's change always stays on top of RSA's edit.
questions.recommended: The editor marks sessions that carry a teacher's change and warns on save; the same rule as EduWave then applies (room-only edit keeps the teacher's change, a new day/time drops it and the teacher is told).

questions.question: A teacher's change only meets the university's version when staff press Apply on a sync. Should staff see, before applying, which teacher changes that sync will drop?
questions.why: Otherwise staff drop a cancellation without knowing, and one bad EduWave page (a section missing for one sync) sends teachers a false 'your change was dropped'.
options: Yes: the check screen lists 'N teacher changes will be dropped' with the classes.
Yes, and staff can tick ones to keep.
No; staff just apply and teachers are told afterwards.
questions.recommended: Yes: the check screen lists 'N teacher changes will be dropped' with the classes.

questions.question: How is the teacher told that the university timetable dropped their change, if their notifications are off?
questions.why: The agreed list says 'the teacher is told' but not where. A teacher without push would never know their cancellation no longer stands.
options: A notification, plus a banner on the teacher home that stays until they dismiss it.
Notification only.
Notification plus an email to their staff address.
questions.recommended: A notification, plus a banner on the teacher home that stays until they dismiss it.

questions.question: An extra class added by a teacher: does the teacher choose lecture, lab or tutorial, and does it count for students' attendance?
questions.why: Classy guesses the type from the room name, so an extra lab in a typed room would show as a lecture. And the student's 'Missed X of Y' either grows with the extra class or does not.
options: Teacher picks the type (default: same as the section's usual); students can mark it missed and it counts in the total.
Teacher picks the type; it does not count for attendance.
Classy guesses the type from the room; it counts for attendance.
questions.recommended: Teacher picks the type (default: same as the section's usual); students can mark it missed and it counts in the total.

questions.question: A cancelled class: does it stop counting in the student's 'Missed 2 of 14', is the reminder before it skipped, and is a 'missed' mark the student already made removed?
questions.why: If the greyed class is still treated as held, students get 'class in 15 minutes' for a cancelled class and their missed percentage is wrong.
options: Yes to all three; a moved class counts once, at its new time.
Skip the reminder, but keep counting it for attendance.
questions.recommended: Yes to all three; a moved class counts once, at its new time.

questions.question: In students' and teachers' phone calendars (Google, Apple, Outlook), what happens to a cancelled class?
questions.why: Calendars refresh slowly (often hours). An entry that silently disappears looks like a glitch; one that stays unmarked sends students to class.
options: It stays, with 'Cancelled:' at the start of its title and the teacher's note inside.
It is removed from the calendar.
questions.recommended: It stays, with 'Cancelled:' at the start of its title and the teacher's note inside.

questions.question: Very small sections: if only one or two Classy students picked a section, the class size and 'N have another class then' point at one person. Show them anyway?
questions.why: The agreed rule is numbers only, no names. With one student, a teacher trying different times can read that student's whole timetable from the clash count.
options: Below 3 students show 'fewer than 3' and no clash count.
Always show the exact numbers.
Below 5 students hide both numbers.
questions.recommended: Below 3 students show 'fewer than 3' and no clash count.

questions.question: For the clash count when moving a class: count only students who have another class then, or also students with a private slot of their own (gym, study) at that time?
questions.why: Counting private slots leaks that a student has something personal then; groups already hide these as plain 'Busy'.
options: Classes only.
Classes and students' own slots.
questions.recommended: Classes only.

questions.question: When an email matches a name and the teacher is linked at once, should anyone be told?
questions.why: Linking at once is agreed, and it comes with the power to cancel classes live. A different staff member with the same first and last name (likely for names like Mohammed Al Balushi) would get that teacher's classes with no human check.
options: Owners get a notification and a dashboard row with a one-tap 'Not them, unlink'; the teacher has full powers meanwhile.
Linked at once but view-only until an owner or RSA taps OK.
Only recorded in the dashboard log; nobody is alerted.
questions.recommended: Owners get a notification and a dashboard row with a one-tap 'Not them, unlink'; the teacher has full powers meanwhile.

questions.question: Nobody has yet checked that Classy's sign-in emails reach GUtech STAFF mailboxes (only student mailboxes are proven), and teachers have no other way in. Should launch wait for a test with one real staff address?
questions.why: Teacher codes are never shown on screen. If the staff mail system filters the email, no teacher can sign in on launch day and there is no fallback.
options: Yes: get one real staff address to try it first (you name the person); launch only after the email arrives.
Launch anyway and fix it if teachers report nothing arrives.
questions.recommended: Yes: get one real staff address to try it first (you name the person); launch only after the email arrives.

questions.question: What do real staff addresses look like for names with 'Al' or three or four words (ali.alhumairi, ali.al-humairi, ali.humairi?), and do any carry a number?
questions.why: 25 of the 83 real names are 'First Al Last'. The auto-link rule was only checked against guessed forms; real examples decide how many teachers link at once versus wait for approval on day one.
options: You send two or three real staff addresses and the rule is tested against them before launch.
Build with the guessed forms; anything else falls to pick-and-approve.
questions.recommended: You send two or three real staff addresses and the rule is tested against them before launch.

questions.question: Can two teachers be linked to the same timetable name?
questions.why: 'One name per teacher' is agreed, but not one teacher per name. If a second person picks a name that is already linked, the picker has to say something.
options: No by default: the second request still goes to staff, flagged 'already linked to x@gutech.edu.om'; staff decide.
Yes, any number of teachers can share a name once approved.
No: the name is hidden from the picker once linked.
questions.recommended: No by default: the second request still goes to staff, flagged 'already linked to x@gutech.edu.om'; staff decide.

questions.question: A teacher is waiting for approval. How do you and RSA find out there is someone to approve?
questions.why: The dashboard has no badges and RSA accounts get no notifications. If nobody happens to open the dashboard, the teacher waits for days on a screen that says 'waiting'.
options: A 'Needs attention' row on the dashboard home, plus a phone notification to owners.
Dashboard row only.
Dashboard row plus an email to an address you choose.
questions.recommended: A 'Needs attention' row on the dashboard home, plus a phone notification to owners.

questions.question: How does a waiting teacher learn they were approved or rejected, and what can a rejected teacher do?
questions.why: A waiting teacher has no notifications yet. Without a message they must keep reopening Classy; a rejected one needs to know whether to try another name.
options: An email to their staff address either way, and the screen updates on next open; a rejected teacher can pick again (up to 3 times), with staff's optional reason shown.
No email; they see it next time they open Classy.
Email on approval only; rejection just returns them to the picker.
questions.recommended: An email to their staff address either way, and the screen updates on next open; a rejected teacher can pick again (up to 3 times), with staff's optional reason shown.

questions.question: While waiting for approval, may a teacher use the free rooms page, reminders and the calendar link?
questions.why: 'Can only view the timetable for the name they picked' could mean strictly that one screen. The free rooms page is open to anyone signed in today.
options: Timetable of the picked name and the free rooms page; no reminders, calendar link, class size or changes.
Strictly the timetable only.
questions.recommended: Timetable of the picked name and the free rooms page; no reminders, calendar link, class size or changes.

questions.question: The student sign-in screen has a small 'Staff? Sign in here' link that leads to the dashboard password login. Teachers are staff and will tap it. What should it do?
questions.why: Students must not see a teacher option, but a teacher who lands on the normal page has no path to /teach and ends up at a username/password form they have no account for.
options: Reword the link to 'Classy team' and add one line on the dashboard login page: 'Teaching staff: go to /teach'.
Leave it as it is; teachers are given the /teach address directly.
Reword to 'Classy team' only, no pointer anywhere.
questions.recommended: Reword the link to 'Classy team' and add one line on the dashboard login page: 'Teaching staff: go to /teach'.

questions.question: After a teacher logs out or their sign-in runs out, the installed app opens the student ID screen (which only takes digits). May the device remember 'a teacher used this' and open the teacher sign-in instead?
questions.why: iPhone notifications only work from the installed app, and that app always opens the normal start page. Without this a teacher on iPhone cannot get back in from the app at all.
options: Yes, remember it on that device, even if a student uses the device next (they can still reach the student sign-in from there).
No; the teacher must type the /teach address again.
questions.recommended: Yes, remember it on that device, even if a student uses the device next (they can still reach the student sign-in from there).

questions.question: How long does a teacher stay signed in?
questions.why: Students stay signed in for 60 days. A signed-in teacher can cancel classes and notify students, and many will use shared lecture-room or office computers.
options: A 'This is my own device' tick at sign-in: ticked = 60 days, not ticked = ends when the browser closes.
60 days, same as students.
7 days for everyone.
questions.recommended: A 'This is my own device' tick at sign-in: ticked = 60 days, not ticked = ends when the browser closes.

questions.question: You sign in with a student ID and have no staff address, so you cannot open /teach yourself. Do you want a way to see the teacher view from the dashboard?
questions.why: Without it the owner cannot check what a teacher sees, help one over the phone, or try the feature before telling staff about it.
options: Yes: 'View as this teacher' for owners, look only, no change buttons.
Yes, with the change buttons (changes logged under the owner).
No.
questions.recommended: Yes: 'View as this teacher' for owners, look only, no change buttons.

questions.question: When an owner or RSA removes a teacher, can that email simply sign in again?
questions.why: Sign-in creates the account on first use. A removed teacher whose email matches a name would be linked again the moment they sign in, with live change powers.
options: No: removal blocks that email until an owner or RSA unblocks it.
Yes, they can come back and go through linking again.
questions.recommended: No: removal blocks that email until an owner or RSA unblocks it.

questions.question: When a teacher is removed, what happens to their cancellations and moves on classes that have not happened yet?
questions.why: If the person was an imposter, those changes must go and students be told. If a real teacher left, their cancelled classes probably are cancelled.
options: The remove screen lists them and staff choose 'undo all (students told)' or 'leave them'.
Always undone, students told the classes are back on.
Always left as they are.
questions.recommended: The remove screen lists them and staff choose 'undo all (students told)' or 'leave them'.

questions.question: Should there be one owner-only switch in the dashboard that turns all teacher changes off at once?
questions.why: Everything ships at once to everyone with no approval on changes. If something goes wrong on launch day (wrong links, mass cancellations), the only other fix is a new deploy.
options: Yes: off = teachers can still see their timetable but cannot cancel, move or add; existing changes stay.
No switch.
questions.recommended: Yes: off = teachers can still see their timetable but cannot cancel, move or add; existing changes stay.

questions.question: Only about four teaching weeks are left this semester (last class 24 December). Launch now, or at the start of next semester?
questions.why: 'Live straight away' is agreed, but this timing was not known then. Launching now means a short real-world trial; added sections and changes all end with the semester.
options: Launch now, as soon as the staff-email test passes.
Build now, launch on the first day of next semester.
questions.recommended: Launch now, as soon as the staff-email test passes.

questions.question: A lecturer who has never signed in to Classy: can students still tap their name? And what about placeholder names like 'CS1 CS1'?
questions.why: On day one almost no teacher has joined. The agreed teacher page (office hours, details, classes this week) would be empty or missing for most names, and placeholders would look like broken people.
options: Every real name is tappable: classes this week, and 'Office hours not added yet'. Placeholders show as 'Lecturer to be announced' and are not tappable.
Names are tappable only once the teacher has joined; placeholders shown as they are.
Every name is tappable, placeholders included.
questions.recommended: Every real name is tappable: classes this week, and 'Office hours not added yet'. Placeholders show as 'Lecturer to be announced' and are not tappable.

questions.question: Office hours are weekly. Should they skip holidays and stop outside the teaching weeks on their own, and can a teacher cancel just one week?
questions.why: Students would otherwise walk to an empty office on a holiday. Cancelling one week is a separate piece of building.
options: Skip holidays and non-teaching weeks automatically; no one-week cancel in this version (the teacher's note can say 'away this week').
Skip automatically, and the teacher can cancel one week with a note.
Show them every week regardless.
questions.recommended: Skip holidays and non-teaching weeks automatically; no one-week cancel in this version (the teacher's note can say 'away this week').

questions.question: When a new semester starts, do a teacher's office hours, office room and note carry over?
questions.why: Office hours usually change with the new teaching timetable. Carried over unchecked, students see last semester's times; wiped, every teacher must retype them.
options: Kept, with a prompt on first open: 'New semester: are your office hours still right?'
Cleared; the teacher sets them again.
Kept with no prompt.
questions.recommended: Kept, with a prompt on first open: 'New semester: are your office hours still right?'

questions.question: Should teachers get a notification when a new semester's timetable is published?
questions.why: Today's announcement says 'Set up your courses' and opens the student setup page, which is wrong for a teacher.
options: Yes, with their own text ('Spring timetable is out: see your classes') opening the teacher home.
No notification for teachers.
questions.recommended: Yes, with their own text ('Spring timetable is out: see your classes') opening the teacher home.

questions.question: Should a teacher be told when the university gives one of their sections to someone else, removes one, or adds a new one under their name?
questions.why: Today only a time/room change of an existing section makes an alert. A teacher could lose or gain a class without hearing about it.
options: Yes, all three.
Only when a section is taken away or removed.
No; only time and room changes.
questions.recommended: Yes, all three.

questions.question: What do teachers get reminders for?
questions.why: The agreed list says reminders before class. Teachers also have own slots and office hours on the same timetable.
options: Classes they teach and their own slots (same as students); not office hours.
Classes only.
Classes, own slots and office hours.
questions.recommended: Classes they teach and their own slots (same as students); not office hours.

questions.question: Batch reps (planner is still off): if a rep already moved a class and the teacher then changes it and later undoes, what comes back? And can a rep publish on a class the teacher already changed?
questions.why: 'Teacher always wins' is agreed, but not what happens after the teacher steps back, nor whether the rep is told their change will be invisible.
options: The rep's version comes back after the teacher's undo; a rep is refused on a session a teacher has changed, with the reason shown.
The university time comes back and the rep's change is removed for good; reps are refused.
The rep's version comes back; reps are only warned.
questions.recommended: The rep's version comes back after the teacher's undo; a rep is refused on a session a teacher has changed, with the reason shown.

questions.question: A rep's cancel makes the class disappear; a teacher's cancel shows it greyed 'Cancelled'. When the planner is switched on, should rep cancels look the same as teacher cancels?
questions.why: Otherwise students see two different pictures for the same event depending on who cancelled.
options: Yes, same greyed 'Cancelled' look, saying who did it.
No, leave rep cancels as they are.
questions.recommended: Yes, same greyed 'Cancelled' look, saying who did it.

questions.question: Should the public timetable link and the staff CSV export show teacher cancellations and moves?
questions.why: The export is fed back in to build the next upload; baking teacher changes into it would turn them into the base timetable.
options: No, both stay the plain university timetable.
Public link shows them; export stays plain.
questions.recommended: No, both stay the plain university timetable.

questions.question: Should 'Delete all data' also delete teachers?
questions.why: Today it keeps dashboard accounts and owners and deletes students. Teacher emails, name links, office details and the change log either survive a wipe or do not, and the confirm text must say which.
options: Yes: teacher accounts, name links, added sections, office hours and the change log all go.
Keep teacher accounts and name links; delete their changes, added sections and office hours.
Keep everything about teachers.
questions.recommended: Yes: teacher accounts, name links, added sections, office hours and the change log all go.

questions.question: Who decides which timetable names are placeholders hidden from the picker?
questions.why: An automatic rule (same word twice, a digit, fewer than two words) catches all eight today, but a new odd name could slip through or a real name be hidden.
options: Automatic rule, and owners/RSA can hide or unhide a name on the Teachers page.
Automatic rule only.
questions.recommended: Automatic rule, and owners/RSA can hide or unhide a name on the Teachers page.

questions.question: Anyone who knows /teach can make Classy email a sign-in code to any @gutech.edu.om address. Is that acceptable?
questions.why: Staff addresses are guessable; strangers could spam staff inboxes from Classy's sender, which is the same sender students' codes depend on. Restricting it would lock out staff whose name is not on the timetable.
options: Accept it, with a much lower limit than students (a few codes per address per day, a small number per network).
Only email addresses that match a timetable name or that an owner added first.
questions.recommended: Accept it, with a much lower limit than students (a few codes per address per day, a small number per network).

questions.question: Which student extras should teachers also get?
questions.why: The teacher home is the student home; each of these either shows or is hidden in the teacher's menu.
options: Colours, share the week as a picture, and 'Report a problem'; no 'Rate Classy' pop-up, no ChatGPT block, no Groups.
Everything students have except Groups and course editing.
None of them.
questions.recommended: Colours, share the week as a picture, and 'Report a problem'; no 'Rate Classy' pop-up, no ChatGPT block, no Groups.

questions.question: Should the dashboard home and Analytics count teachers separately?
questions.why: Otherwise teacher traffic is counted as 'staff' or mixed into student numbers.
options: Separately: 'teachers signed in' and 'teacher changes this week'; student numbers stay students only.
Leave teachers out of the numbers.
questions.recommended: Separately: 'teachers signed in' and 'teacher changes this week'; student numbers stay students only.

questions.question: How long does the dashboard log of teacher changes keep entries?
questions.why: It must survive a section being dropped by a sync, and staff may want last semester's history after a new one is published.
options: The whole semester, and it stays viewable (by picking that semester) after a new one is published.
Current semester only; cleared when a new one is published.
questions.recommended: The whole semester, and it stays viewable (by picking that semester) after a new one is published.

contradictions: Item 3 against items 2 and 5: names need owner/RSA approval, but changes are live with no approval. If a self-added section carries change powers, any staff email can cancel any class in the university and the name approval protects nothing. If it carries none, the real teachers of the 20 sections listed under placeholder names (12 of 15 lab sections) can never change their own class.

Item 2 says a waiting teacher can 'only view the timetable for the name they picked', but item 3 lets teachers add sections and item 4 gives a free rooms page; the free rooms page is already open to anyone signed in (FreeRooms.cs:93). The list does not say which of these a waiting teacher gets.

Item 2 assumes every teacher either matches a name or can pick one. Staff whose name is not on the timetable (lab assistants behind 'CS1 CS1', new staff, staff who teach nothing) have nothing to pick, and placeholders are hidden from the picker by the same item.

Item 5 says a cancelled class stays on the timetable greyed out. Today the only cancel mechanism removes the date and the web app hides it (slots.ts onDate). A rep's cancel (item 10) would vanish while a teacher's shows greyed, so students see two different pictures for the same event.

Item 5 says 'one future session at a time', but 67 of 306 sections are one real class listed under two or three course codes. Cancelling one session on one section leaves the other codes' students seeing the class as on.
Item 5 'undo until the class starts' has no single meaning for a moved class (old start or new start), and allows un-cancelling a class minutes before it begins, after students were told it was off.
Item 5 lets the teacher pick any new time, but the week view has only six fixed class slots and draws anything else in the nearest row, possibly on top of another class.

Item 6 says the teacher's change is dropped when EduWave 'moves' the session. The existing overlay key includes the room, and room-only changes are the commonest university change; copied as is, a cancelled class would show as on again after a room edit. The existing mechanism also drops silently, while item 6 says the teacher is told.

Item 6 speaks as if EduWave changes arrive on their own. They only take effect when an owner or RSA presses Apply on a sync, and RSA can also hand-edit a session; the list says nothing about what staff see or decide at that moment.

Item 7 says students are told 'at once'. The notification worker runs every 30 seconds, the open app only refetches on load or when coming back online, calendar feeds lag by hours, and students with change alerts off or no notifications get nothing but the mark.

Item 1 says entry is a direct address only and students never see a teacher option. But the installed app always opens '/', log-out lands on the student ID screen (digits only), and that screen's 'Staff? Sign in here' link goes to the dashboard password login. A signed-out teacher has no way back to /teach from the app.
Item 8 says numbers only, no names. In sections with one or two Classy students, class size and the clash count identify one person and, tried slot by slot, reveal that student's timetable.

Item 9 says students tap the teacher's name to open a teacher page. Teachers are free-text names; on launch day almost none has an account, and placeholder names are not people. The list does not say what the page is for a name with no teacher behind it.

Item 11 lets staff remove a teacher, but sign-in creates the account on first use and item 2 links a matching email at once, so a removed teacher is back with full powers on their next sign-in unless removal also blocks.

Item 12 says live for everyone at once, but teacher sign-in works only by email, delivery to staff mailboxes has never been tested, and the owner has no staff address so cannot sign in at /teach to check anything before or after launch.

Item 10 (rep events on the teacher's timetable, teacher wins) depends on the planner, which is switched off in production. That rule will ship with no real use, and teacher changes must not be built on the planner path or they would do nothing while it is off.

Item 4 gives teachers the same home as students, which assumes one class per course. 26 of 91 teachers teach several sections of one course, so course pages, session links and reminder links keyed by course would open the wrong section.

risks.risk: A person who is not the teacher gets change powers: a same-name staff member is auto-linked, a wrong name is approved, or a self-added section carries powers. They can cancel real classes with a notification to every Classy student in the section.
risks.mitigation: Change powers only for approved names and approved sections; owners alerted on every auto-link with one-tap unlink; every change in the dashboard log with undo; an owner-only switch that turns all teacher changes off.

risks.risk: Sign-in emails do not reach staff mailboxes, so no teacher can sign in on launch day and there is no other way in.
risks.mitigation: Test with one real staff mailbox before launch; on the code screen show 'check junk' and who to contact; do not announce to staff until the test passes.

risks.risk: A cancelled class shows as on again after a routine EduWave room change or a staff hand edit, and students turn up.
risks.mitigation: Match a teacher's change on section + date + start time, never on the room or on meeting ids; drop only when the day/time changes or the session disappears; show staff the changes a sync will drop before they apply.

risks.risk: One bad EduWave page (a section missing for one sync) deletes the section, taking the teacher's changes and added sections with it and sending a false 'your change was dropped'. The section comes back next sync as a new row.
risks.mitigation: Keep a text copy (course code + section number) on every teacher row and re-attach when the section returns; list affected teacher changes on the sync check screen.

risks.risk: Combined classes: a change on one course code leaves the other codes' students with the class as on; the teacher sees their own class as a clash and as 'room taken'.
risks.mitigation: Group sections with the same teacher, date, time and room into one block and apply changes to the whole group.

risks.risk: The timetable page and the reminders/calendar/free-rooms/groups code are two separate paths. If only one learns about teacher changes, the app says Cancelled while a reminder still fires, or the reverse.
risks.mitigation: Put the overlay in the one shared schedule builder and make the timetable endpoint use it; tests that check every surface for each change kind with the planner off.

risks.risk: A greyed cancelled class is still treated as a real class: 'Next in 12 min', counted in attendance, flagged as a clash, drawn in the shared week picture.
risks.mitigation: Send cancelled sessions as display-only records; exclude them from next/live logic, clashes, attendance totals and reminders.

risks.risk: Students who keep the app open, have alerts off, or rely on their phone calendar do not see a late cancellation in time.
risks.mitigation: Refetch the timetable when the app comes back to the front; show cancellations on the home for today; keep the calendar entry with 'Cancelled:' in the title; tell teachers in the cancel screen how many students have notifications on.

risks.risk: Shared computers: a teacher stays signed in for 60 days on a lecture-room PC with the power to cancel classes; the next person on that browser can also see the previous person's saved timetable offline and receive their notifications.
risks.mitigation: 'This is my own device' tick controlling how long the sign-in lasts; stamp the saved timetable with its owner and clear it when the person changes; sign the previous person out properly (releasing the device's notifications) before a /teach sign-in.

risks.risk: A signed-out teacher on the installed app lands on the student ID screen with no route to /teach; on iPhone that app is the only way to get notifications.
risks.mitigation: Remember on the device that a teacher used it and open the teacher sign-in; point teachers to /teach from the dashboard login page.

risks.risk: A waiting teacher is never approved because nobody notices the request.
risks.mitigation: 'Needs attention' row on the dashboard home plus a notification to owners; email the teacher when approved or rejected.

risks.risk: Class size and clash count expose one student in very small sections.
risks.mitigation: Hide exact numbers below a minimum; count classes only, never private slots; no numbers for sections a teacher only watches.

risks.risk: Linking by name spelling: EduWave re-spells or reassigns a name and a teacher's timetable empties silently, or a section (with change powers) passes to whoever now carries the name.
risks.mitigation: Compare names ignoring case and spacing; record old and new instructor at apply time; alert both teachers; flag probable re-spellings to staff for one-tap re-link instead of following automatically.

risks.risk: Removing a teacher does not stick, and their live cancellations stay on students' timetables with nobody owning them.
risks.mitigation: Removal blocks the email; the remove screen lists their upcoming changes and makes staff choose undo or keep.

risks.risk: Teachers end up on student pages that cannot work for them (course page by course id, group invites, setup, 'Pick my courses' empty state), or see students' notes.
risks.mitigation: Separate teacher endpoints that never send notes; section-keyed session links; teacher wording for every empty state; guards that send a teacher to /teach.

risks.risk: Everything ships in one push to a live site with real students; a migration that succeeds but is wrong cannot be rolled back without losing what students did afterwards.
risks.mitigation: Additive tables only (no changes to existing student tables); full test run before the push; the owner switch for teacher changes; a 'first deploy with teachers' note with the checks to run after deploy.

risks.risk: Notification noise: a teacher change, its undo, an RSA edit and a sync on the same class each notify the same students, and later ones replace earlier ones on the phone.
risks.mitigation: One notification per session that updates in place (tag per session, not per section); undo before sending cancels both; suppress the university 'changed' alert when it only confirms the teacher's own change.

risks.risk: Anyone who knows /teach can use Classy to send code emails to guessed staff addresses, hurting the sender reputation students' sign-in depends on, or use up a teacher's daily code allowance.
risks.mitigation: A much lower per-network limit for teacher code requests than for students; identical answers for known and unknown addresses; never show a teacher's code on screen in any mode.

questions.question: When a teacher adds a section that is not under their name, what can they do with it?
questions.why: Class changes go live with no approval and notify students at once. If added sections carry full powers, any staff email could cancel any class in the university and the name approval step means nothing. If they are view-only, the 20 sections listed under placeholder names like 'CS1 CS1' (12 of the 15 labs) can never be cancelled or moved by their real teacher.
options: See it only (timetable, reminders, calendar); never change it
See it at once; cancel, move and re-room only after an owner or RSA approves that section
Full powers at once, no approval
questions.recommended: See it at once; cancel, move and re-room only after an owner or RSA approves that section

questions.question: About one lesson in eight is one real class listed under two or three course codes (for example BE1101, IBSM1101 and LOG1101 section 1: same teacher, time and room). Should Classy treat it as one class for the teacher?
questions.why: If each code stays separate, cancelling one leaves the other codes' students seeing the class as on, the teacher sees three stacked blocks flagged as a clash, the 'room is taken' warning points at the teacher's own class, and the class size is a third of the real room.
options: Yes: one block, one tap changes it for all the codes, class size is the combined total
No: each code is separate and the teacher changes each one
questions.recommended: Yes: one block, one tap changes it for all the codes, class size is the combined total

questions.question: The university gives a section to a different teacher mid-semester. What happens to the first teacher's upcoming cancels and moves on it?
questions.why: If they are dropped, a class students were told is cancelled silently comes back. If they stay and only staff can undo, the new teacher is stuck with someone else's cancellation. It happened to ENG4135 section 2 this month.
options: They stay; the new teacher (and staff) can undo them; both teachers are told
They are dropped; students are told the class is back on; both teachers are told
They stay; only owners and RSA can undo them
questions.recommended: They stay; the new teacher (and staff) can undo them; both teachers are told

questions.question: The university changes only the ROOM of a session the teacher already cancelled or moved (same day and time). Does the teacher's change stay?
questions.why: Room-only changes are by far the most common university change (16 of 18 between two real exports). If they count as 'EduWave moved it', a cancelled class shows as on again after students were told it was cancelled.
options: It stays; only a change of date or time, or the class disappearing, drops it
It is dropped and the teacher is told, like any other university change
questions.recommended: It stays; only a change of date or time, or the class disappearing, drops it

questions.question: After an owner or RSA removes a teacher, can that email come back?
questions.why: Sign-in creates the account on first use. Without a rule, a removed person signs in again and, if their email matches a name, is linked again at once with full change powers, so 'remove' does nothing.
options: Blocked until an owner or RSA unblocks the email
Can sign in again, but is never linked automatically: always waits for approval, shown as 'removed before'
Can come back freely like a removed student
questions.recommended: Can sign in again, but is never linked automatically: always waits for approval, shown as 'removed before'

questions.question: A teacher is removed (or a name is taken off them) while some of their cancels and moves are still live. What happens to those changes?
questions.why: If the person was the wrong person, their changes must go and students be told. If a real teacher simply left, their cancellations may be true and undoing them sends students to empty rooms.
options: Staff choose at removal: a tick box 'also undo their N live changes' (students are told the class is back on)
Always undone, students told
Always left in force; staff undo one by one in the log
questions.recommended: Staff choose at removal: a tick box 'also undo their N live changes' (students are told the class is back on)

questions.question: Staff whose name is not on the timetable at all (for example lab assistants teaching the 'CS1 CS1' lab sections) sign in at /teach. What happens?
questions.why: They have no name to pick, so the agreed name flow gives them nothing. Either they are turned away or adding sections is their only way in, which needs its own waiting state.
options: Let in: they pick sections, each one waits for owner or RSA approval; until then they only see free rooms and the sections they asked for
Turned away with 'your name is not on the timetable, contact the Classy team'
Owners or RSA must add them by hand from the dashboard first
questions.recommended: Let in: they pick sections, each one waits for owner or RSA approval; until then they only see free rooms and the sections they asked for

questions.question: Can a teacher who is still waiting for their name to be approved add other courses or sections?
questions.why: The agreed rule says a waiting teacher can only view the timetable for the name they picked. Adding sections while waiting either breaks that rule or has to be blocked.
options: No: adding sections opens only after the name is approved
Yes, to view only; any change power still waits for approval
questions.recommended: Yes, to view only; any change power still waits for approval

questions.question: When a teacher 'picks a course', what do they get?
questions.why: The request says 'courses or sections'. A whole-course pick on a 19-section course like LS1003 fills the timetable and reminders with other people's classes, and decides whether sections the university adds later appear by themselves.
options: Sections are always chosen one by one (the course is just how you find them)
A course pick means all its sections as they are today
A course pick means all its sections, including ones added later
questions.recommended: Sections are always chosen one by one (the course is just how you find them)

questions.question: Two teachers end up on the same section (one named by the university, one who added it, or two lab assistants on one placeholder section). Who can undo or replace a change made on it?
questions.why: Co-teachers may disagree: one cancels, the other un-cancels. Students get both notifications. The rule decides who has the last word.
options: Either teacher on the section can undo or replace it; the one who made it is told
Only the teacher who made it, plus owners and RSA
The named teacher can undo anyone's; an added teacher only their own
questions.recommended: Either teacher on the section can undo or replace it; the one who made it is told

questions.question: When another teacher adds a section that is under someone's name, is the named teacher told?
questions.why: Otherwise a named teacher can find their class cancelled by a colleague they did not know was attached to it.
options: Yes, a notification when the other teacher is approved for it
No, only owners and RSA see it
questions.recommended: Yes, a notification when the other teacher is approved for it

questions.question: Do students see a teacher who added a section by hand?
questions.why: Decides whose name, office hours and teacher page appear on the class, and whether the placeholder 'CS1 CS1' is ever replaced by a real person.
options: Yes once approved: shown next to the university name; a placeholder name is replaced by the real teacher
Only when the university name is a placeholder
Never: students keep seeing only the university name
questions.recommended: Yes once approved: shown next to the university name; a placeholder name is replaced by the real teacher

questions.question: Can a teacher say 'this one is not mine' for a section the university lists under their name?
questions.why: In the real data one name is listed in two rooms at the same time on 64 slots, so the listed person is not always teaching. Without this, their timetable and reminders show classes they do not teach.
options: Yes: hidden from their own timetable and reminders, and staff are told
Yes, and it also disappears from their teacher page for students
No: everything under the name always shows
questions.recommended: Yes: hidden from their own timetable and reminders, and staff are told

questions.question: An extra class for a course with several sections: who is it for?
questions.why: 26 of 91 teachers teach several sections of one course. One section only means entering a shared revision class several times; all sections would reach other teachers' students.
options: The teacher ticks one or more of the sections they are allowed to change
Always exactly one section
Every section of the course, including other teachers'
questions.recommended: The teacher ticks one or more of the sections they are allowed to change

questions.question: The university re-spells a teacher's name (so it no longer matches their link). What should Classy do?
questions.why: The teacher's timetable goes empty with no error. Following automatically cannot tell a new spelling from a real replacement: Ahmad/Ahmed and Mohamed/Mohammad/Mohammed are different people in the real list.
options: Flag it to owners and RSA with a one-tap 'same person' button; the teacher sees 'your name changed, waiting for the Classy team'
Follow automatically when the same sections simply carry one new name
Do nothing: the teacher picks their name again and waits for approval
questions.recommended: Flag it to owners and RSA with a one-tap 'same person' button; the teacher sees 'your name changed, waiting for the Classy team'

questions.question: A teacher picks a new time on a day off, a Friday or Saturday, or outside the teaching weeks. Warn or refuse?
questions.why: The agreed rule is 'warn, never block' for clashes and rooms, but nothing is said for dates. Make-up classes on a weekend or holiday are real; a slip of the finger onto a holiday is also real.
options: Warn clearly and allow
Refuse days off and dates outside the teaching weeks; warn for weekends
Refuse all of them
questions.recommended: Warn clearly and allow

questions.question: What times can a class be moved to, or an extra class added at?
questions.why: The week view has only six fixed rows (08:00, 09:45, 11:30, 13:15, 15:00, 16:45). A class at another time is drawn in the nearest row and can sit on top of another class.
options: The six standard slots as quick picks, plus any time typed in
Only the six standard slots
Any time, no quick picks
questions.recommended: The six standard slots as quick picks, plus any time typed in

questions.question: How short can the notice be when a class is moved to a new time?
questions.why: A teacher could move a class to a time that starts in ten minutes; students get a notification they cannot act on. The agreed list only says the session must be in the future.
options: Any future time, with a warning when it starts in under 2 hours
The new time must be at least 2 hours away
The new time must be on a later day
questions.recommended: Any future time, with a warning when it starts in under 2 hours

questions.question: 'Undo until the class starts': for a MOVED class, which start counts?
questions.why: A Monday class moved to Wednesday: undoing on Tuesday would put the class back in the past. A class moved earlier: after it has been held at the new time, undo would bring back the old slot as a second class.
options: Whichever comes first, the old time or the new time
The old (original) time
The new time
questions.recommended: Whichever comes first, the old time or the new time

questions.question: A teacher cancels a class, students are told, then the teacher undoes it shortly before it starts. Allow?
questions.why: Students who were told 'cancelled' may already have left campus; a class brought back ten minutes before start costs them an absence.
options: Allowed until the class starts, with a warning to the teacher ('students were told it was cancelled 3 hours ago') and a 'back on' notification
Undoing a cancel stops 2 hours before the class
Allowed, no warning
questions.recommended: Allowed until the class starts, with a warning to the teacher ('students were told it was cancelled 3 hours ago') and a 'back on' notification

questions.question: A session already has a teacher change and the teacher wants another (move it again, fix the room, cancel a moved class). How?
questions.why: Decides whether there is one change per session that gets edited, or an undo-then-redo that sends students 'back on' followed by a second change.
options: Change it in place: the new version replaces the old one and students get one notification with the latest state
Must undo first, then make a new change
questions.recommended: Change it in place: the new version replaces the old one and students get one notification with the latest state

questions.question: A section has two sessions on the same day (it happens on 395 section-days, often a double lecture or lecture plus lab). How does cancel or move work?
questions.why: A teacher who is away means both. One at a time means two actions and two notifications; treating them as one makes it impossible to cancel only the second half.
options: One at a time, with a tick box 'also the other session that day'
Strictly one at a time
Sessions that follow straight after each other are always treated as one
questions.recommended: One at a time, with a tick box 'also the other session that day'

questions.question: When a class is moved, what stays at the old time on students' timetables?
questions.why: The agreed list says a cancelled class stays greyed out, but not what a moved class leaves behind. Students who look at the old slot out of habit see nothing and assume it is on, or assume it vanished.
options: A greyed block 'Moved to Tue 10:00' at the old time, plus the class at the new time with a Moved mark
Only the class at the new time with a Moved mark
questions.recommended: A greyed block 'Moved to Tue 10:00' at the old time, plus the class at the new time with a Moved mark

questions.question: The teacher changed a room and the university later lists a different room for that same session. Which room do students see?
questions.why: Both are 'official' in someone's eyes. Picking the wrong one sends a class to the wrong room.
options: The teacher's room stays; the teacher is told the university now lists another room
The university's newer room wins; the teacher is told their change was dropped
questions.recommended: The teacher's room stays; the teacher is told the university now lists another room

questions.question: An RSA edits by hand a session that a teacher has already cancelled or moved. What happens?
questions.why: The section editor rewrites the whole class list and today shows nothing about changes on top, so an RSA fixing one room could wipe a teacher's cancellation without knowing it existed, and students get two different notifications.
options: RSA sees the teacher's change marked on the session and a warning on save; after that the same rule as a university change applies
RSA must undo the teacher's change first
RSA's edit always wins silently
questions.recommended: RSA sees the teacher's change marked on the session and a warning on save; after that the same rule as a university change applies

questions.question: Before staff press Apply on a sync or upload, should they see which teacher changes it will drop?
questions.why: A teacher's change only meets the university's version when staff apply. One bad EduWave page can make a section look dropped and send teachers a false 'your change was dropped'.
options: Yes: a count and list in the preview; applying drops them
Yes, and staff can tick ones to keep
No list
questions.recommended: Yes: a count and list in the preview; applying drops them

questions.question: When an owner or RSA undoes a teacher's change from the log, is the teacher told, and must staff give a reason?
questions.why: A teacher who is not told will think the class is still cancelled. A required reason slows staff down in an emergency.
options: Teacher is told; reason optional and shown to the teacher
Teacher is told; reason required
Teacher is not told
questions.recommended: Teacher is told; reason optional and shown to the teacher

questions.question: Does an extra class added by a teacher count for students' own attendance count ('Missed 2 of 14')?
questions.why: Classes added by batch reps count today. If teacher extras count, an optional revision session raises the total; if not, a real make-up class cannot be marked missed.
options: Yes, like any class
No, extra classes never count
The teacher chooses when adding it
questions.recommended: Yes, like any class

questions.question: In students' phone calendars (Google, Apple), what happens to a cancelled class?
questions.why: Calendars refresh slowly. A removed event just vanishes; a kept one marked Cancelled matches the greyed class in the app but clutters the calendar.
options: Kept, with 'Cancelled:' at the start of the title
Removed from the calendar
questions.recommended: Kept, with 'Cancelled:' at the start of the title

questions.question: For very small sections (one or two Classy students), should the teacher see the class size and 'N students have another class then'?
questions.why: With one student in a section, '1 has another class then', checked slot by slot, reveals that one person's whole timetable even though no name is shown.
options: Class size always shown; the clash count is hidden when fewer than 5 Classy students picked the section
Always show both
Hide both under 5 students
questions.recommended: Class size always shown; the clash count is hidden when fewer than 5 Classy students picked the section

questions.question: You (the owner) sign in with a student ID and have no staff address. Do you want to open the teacher view for any name from the dashboard?
questions.why: Without it nobody on the Classy team can see what a teacher sees or check a complaint. With change buttons, owners could change any class as if they were the teacher.
options: Yes, view only (changes are undone from the log)
Yes, with the change buttons; each change is logged under the owner
No
questions.recommended: Yes, view only (changes are undone from the log)

questions.question: A student who also teaches (a teaching assistant or lab demonstrator with only a student email) cannot sign in at /teach. Support them?
questions.why: Teacher sign-in only accepts staff addresses. If student demonstrators run labs, those labs can never have a teacher in Classy.
options: Not in this update
Owners can give a student account teaching rights for chosen sections
questions.recommended: Not in this update

questions.question: A new semester is published. What happens to the sections a teacher added by hand?
questions.why: New semesters have all-new section rows. Carrying picks over by course code could attach a teacher (and their change powers) to a section someone else now teaches.
options: Start empty; last semester's are offered as suggestions and need approval again
Carried over automatically where the same course and section number exist
questions.recommended: Start empty; last semester's are offered as suggestions and need approval again

questions.question: How long does a teacher stay signed in, given many will use shared lecture-room or office computers?
questions.why: Students stay signed in 60 days. A teacher's sign-in left open on a shared PC lets the next person cancel classes.
options: 60 days, with a 'shared computer' tick at sign-in that ends it when the browser closes
60 days like students
7 days for all teachers
questions.recommended: 60 days, with a 'shared computer' tick at sign-in that ends it when the browser closes

questions.question: Do you want one owner-only switch that turns off all teacher class changes at once?
questions.why: The rollout is live for everyone on day one. If a wrong person gets linked or a bug sends wrong cancellations, the only other stop is a new deploy.
options: Yes: switch off stops new changes; existing ones stay until undone
Yes: switch off also hides all existing teacher changes from students
No switch
questions.recommended: Yes: switch off stops new changes; existing ones stay until undone

questions.question: A person who is both dashboard staff (RSA or owner) and a teacher can hold only one sign-in per browser and must sign out of one to use the other. OK?
questions.why: The site keeps one sign-in per browser. A quick switcher is extra work and extra risk of mixing identities.
options: Fine as it is
Add a quick switch between the two
questions.recommended: Fine as it is

questions.question: The new time clashes with another class the same teacher teaches. Warn or refuse?
questions.why: Follows the agreed 'warn, never block' rule unless you want the teacher's own clash to be a hard stop.
options: Warn ('You teach CS 2101 then') and allow
Refuse
questions.recommended: Warn ('You teach CS 2101 then') and allow

questions.question: Moving a class to a time that has already passed, or changing a class that has already started: refused?
questions.why: The agreed list says 'one future session at a time'. A room locked five minutes into class is the one case where a late room change might be wanted.
options: Refused in both cases
Refused, except a room change is allowed until the class ends
questions.recommended: Refused in both cases

questions.question: For a class that repeats weekly with no dates, a cancel or move applies only to the one week picked, and is refused on a day off (no class that day). OK?
questions.why: All real data is dated today, but the sample and test data are weekly, so the rule must exist.
options: Yes
Also offer 'every week from now on'
questions.recommended: Yes

questions.question: When a change is undone, students get a 'back on' notification; if it is undone before the first notification went out, nothing is sent. OK?
questions.why: Avoids a 'cancelled' and 'back on' pair for a mistake corrected within seconds.
options: Yes
Always send both
questions.recommended: Yes

questions.question: Two people act on the same session at the same moment (two teachers, or a teacher and staff). Which wins?
questions.why: Last-one-wins can silently replace a colleague's change made seconds earlier.
options: The second is refused and shown the change that is already there
The last one wins and the other is told
questions.recommended: The second is refused and shown the change that is already there

questions.question: When one teacher on a shared section cancels or moves a class, the other teacher on it gets a notification. OK?
questions.why: Otherwise a co-teacher turns up to a class their colleague cancelled.
options: Yes
No
questions.recommended: Yes

questions.question: If the university timetable later shows exactly what the teacher did (class now officially at the new time, or the extra class now officially listed), the teacher's change quietly merges into it with no 'dropped' message and no second alert to students. OK?
questions.why: Otherwise the teacher gets a confusing 'your change was dropped' and students a duplicate 'changed' alert for something that did not change for them.
options: Yes, merge quietly
Tell the teacher anyway
questions.recommended: Yes, merge quietly

questions.question: A section disappears in one sync and comes back in the next (EduWave glitch). The teacher's hand-added link is re-attached by course code and section number; their dropped changes are not restored and the teacher is told once. OK?
questions.why: A returning section is a new row; without re-attaching, hand-added sections vanish for good after a glitch.
options: Yes
Restore the dropped changes too
Re-attach nothing
questions.recommended: Yes

questions.question: A teacher's name has no classes left after a sync (two real names have a single class row). They keep their account, office hours and link, with an empty timetable. OK?
questions.why: The alternative sends them back to 'pick your name' and approval for what may be a one-day glitch.
options: Yes, keep the account and link
Back to pick-a-name
questions.recommended: Yes, keep the account and link

questions.question: Teachers are told when the university removes one of their sections, adds a new section under their name, or gives one of theirs to someone else. OK?
questions.why: Today only a time, room or instructor change of an existing section raises an alert; added and removed sections alert nobody.
options: Yes
Only time and room changes, as for students
questions.recommended: Yes

questions.question: A batch rep already changed a session and the teacher then changes it. The teacher's wins; if the teacher undoes theirs, the rep's version comes back; the rep sees 'replaced by the lecturer' in their planner but gets no notification; a teacher cannot change classes or exams a rep added. OK?
questions.why: The planner is switched off in production, so this only matters on the day it is turned on; teacher changes themselves work whether the planner is on or off.
options: Yes
When the teacher undoes, go back to the university's original instead
questions.recommended: Yes

questions.question: A second staff email claims a name that is already linked to a teacher (same-name colleague, or the same person's alias address). It always waits for approval and staff see both. OK?
questions.why: Auto-linking a second person to an already linked name would give a same-name colleague the teacher's classes at once.
options: Yes, always needs approval
Refuse the second email outright
questions.recommended: Yes, always needs approval

questions.question: All times are Oman time everywhere, whatever the phone's time zone; 'has the class started' is judged by the Oman clock. OK?
questions.why: A teacher abroad at a conference would otherwise see shifted times or be able to undo a class that has already started in Muscat.
options: Yes, Oman time only
Show times in the device's own time zone
questions.recommended: Yes, Oman time only

questions.question: When a teacher's device is offline, the cancel, move, room and extra-class buttons are switched off (nothing is saved up to send later). OK?
questions.why: A queued cancel sent hours later could land after the class started or on top of a newer timetable.
options: Yes, buttons off while offline
Save the change and send it when back online
questions.recommended: Yes, buttons off while offline

questions.question: A student's app that was offline or left open may not show a new Cancelled mark. Classy will refresh the timetable whenever the app comes back to the front and show 'updated at 10:42' on a saved copy. OK?
questions.why: Today the app only refetches when opened fresh or when the connection returns, so a student with alerts off could miss a cancellation for hours.
options: Yes
Leave as today
questions.recommended: Yes

questions.question: A cancelled class stops counting in the student's attendance total, its reminder is skipped, and an 'I missed this' mark already put on it is dropped. A moved class counts once, at its new time. OK?
questions.why: Otherwise a cancelled class inflates 'of Y' or leaves a missed mark on a class that never happened.
options: Yes
Keep counting cancelled classes
questions.recommended: Yes

questions.question: For a moved class the type (lecture, lab, tutorial) stays as it was; for an extra class the teacher picks it, pre-set to the section's usual type. OK?
questions.why: Classy guesses the type from the room name today, so a lab moved to a typed room or 'to be announced' would turn into a lecture in colour and label.
options: Yes
Keep guessing from the room name
questions.recommended: Yes

questions.question: The clash count when moving counts only students' other classes, never their private own slots (gym, study). OK?
questions.why: Own slots are private; groups already show them only as 'Busy'.
options: Yes, classes only
Count own slots too
questions.recommended: Yes, classes only

questions.question: After a teacher logs out or their sign-in runs out, the device remembers 'a teacher used this' and opens the teacher sign-in instead of the student ID screen. OK?
questions.why: The installed app (needed for iPhone notifications) opens on the student screen, which by your rule has no teacher option, so a teacher would be stuck there.
options: Yes
No: teachers must type /teach again
questions.recommended: Yes

questions.question: The teacher change log stays for the whole semester and remains viewable under the old semester after a new one is published; office hours and details carry over to the new semester. OK?
questions.why: Name links carry over by spelling, but everything tied to a section ends with the semester; the log and office hours need a stated rule.
options: Yes
Clear office hours each semester
questions.recommended: Yes

questions.question: Office hours are skipped automatically on days off and outside the teaching weeks; a teacher cannot cancel a single week's office hours in this update. OK?
questions.why: A per-week cancel for office hours is a second change system; skipping it keeps this update smaller.
options: Yes
Add cancel-one-week for office hours now
questions.recommended: Yes

questions.question: The public timetable link and the staff CSV export stay as the plain university timetable, without teacher cancels and moves. OK?
questions.why: The export is fed back into the next upload, so teacher changes baked into it would become permanent timetable data.
options: Yes, keep them pure
Show teacher changes on the public link
questions.recommended: Yes, keep them pure

contradictions: Item 3 (teacher picks other sections) plus item 5 (changes live at once, no approval) cancels out item 2 (owner or RSA approves the name): any staff email could add any section and cancel it with a live notification, unless added sections are view-only or approved one by one.

Item 5 says a cancelled class stays on the timetable greyed out. Today the only cancel mechanism (excludedDates, web/src/lib/slots.ts onDate) makes the class vanish, and that is how batch reps' cancels will look when the planner is on. Teacher cancels and rep cancels would look different unless reps' are changed too. Old cached app versions will also only understand 'vanish', so the server must keep sending the excluded date and send the greyed mark separately.

Item 5 says 'one session at a time', but about 12% of teacher time-slots are one real lesson stored as two or three sections under different course codes. One real cancellation needs two or three changes made together, or students of the other codes still see the class as on.

Item 6 says the teacher's change is dropped 'if EduWave later moves or drops that session'. Classy only learns this when staff press Apply on a pending sync (hours later), and the existing way of recognising a session (PlannerEngine.Fingerprint) includes the room, so the commonest university change (room only) would count as 'moved' and bring back a cancelled class.

Item 7 says students are told 'at once'. In the code change alerts go out from a worker every 30 seconds, one device at a time; the open app does not refetch (only on fresh open or reconnect); calendar feeds refresh hourly at best; students with change alerts off get only the mark.

Item 5 'undo until the class starts' has no single meaning for a moved class (old start or new start), and together with item 7 it allows un-cancelling a class minutes before it starts, after students were told it was cancelled.

Item 10 (rep events on the teacher's timetable, teacher wins over rep) depends on the planner, which is switched off in production: nothing will show and the 'teacher wins' code will ship unused. The planner's own 'one adjustment per session' check only knows planner events, so a rep could publish over a teacher's change and be told it is live.

Item 1 says students never see a teacher option, but the installed app starts at '/', log-out goes to /login, and the student screen's 'Staff? Sign in here' link leads to the dashboard password login. A signed-out teacher lands on a digits-only student ID screen with no way to /teach.

Item 2 links a matching email 'at once' and item 11 lets staff 'remove a teacher', but accounts are created at sign-in: a removed teacher signs in again and is auto-linked again unless a block or 'no auto-link' flag is stored.
Item 8 promises 'a number only, no names', but class size is the count of Classy students who picked the section, often 1 to 3. A clash count on such a section points at one identifiable student.

Item 9 (tap the teacher's name for their page) and item 2 (one name per teacher) assume the name on a section is the person teaching. Section.Instructor is one free-text string: a second teacher cannot exist by name (the importer keeps the first), 20 sections carry placeholder names, and one name is listed in two rooms at once on 64 slots.
Item 5 lets the teacher pick any new time, but the week view has six fixed rows; a class at another time is drawn in the nearest row and can cover another class.

Item 4 gives teachers own slots, reminders and a calendar feed, but CustomSlot, PushSubscription and the calendar token all require a Student row, and every /api/me endpoint reads Students by the bare id in the cookie. Teachers cannot reuse them without separate tables and endpoints, or teacher number 7 would read student number 7's data.

Item 12 (live for everyone at once) versus two facts: teacher sign-in can only work by real email (the on-screen test code must never be shown for teachers) and delivery to @gutech.edu.om staff mailboxes has never been tested; and the owner, who signs in with a student ID, cannot sign in at /teach to check anything.

Item 7 says teachers get change alerts when the university timetable changes one of their classes, but alerts are sent up to 30 seconds after the change to whoever matches the section then. A teacher just replaced as instructor no longer matches, and new or removed sections raise no alert at all today.

risks.risk: Hand-added sections with live change powers let any staff email cancel any class, with a push to students, without anyone approving.
risks.mitigation: Per-section approval before change rights; check the right on every write endpoint (linked name or approved section), not only at sign-in; log every change; owner kill switch; test that a pending teacher and an unapproved section get 403 on every change route.

risks.risk: Combined classes (one lesson under 2-3 course codes) are changed for one code only; other students still see the class as on, and the teacher sees stacked blocks marked as a clash.
risks.mitigation: Group sections by same teacher, date, start and end; one teacher action writes one change row per section with a shared group id; class size and clash count summed over the group; the room-taken check ignores the group's own sections; tests with a three-code class.

risks.risk: Meeting ids are deleted and recreated whenever anything in a section changes (ScheduleImport.cs:414-418, AdminEndpoints.cs:335-336), so a change stored by meeting id is lost on the next sync.
risks.mitigation: Store section id + original date + start time, plus text copies of course code, section number and the original end and room; never Meeting.Id; re-sync tests where only the room or only the instructor changes.

risks.risk: Two places build what a student sees (GET /me/timetable and StudentSchedule.ForAsync), and both only apply overlays when the planner flag is on. Patch one and the app says Cancelled while reminders, calendar, free rooms or group free time say the class is on, or the reverse.
risks.mitigation: One shared loader for teacher changes applied in both paths regardless of the planner switch; tests asserting timetable, reminders, .ics, free rooms, groups and absences agree with the planner off.

risks.risk: A greyed cancelled class kept in the session list is treated as real: 'Next in 12 min', live ring, clash pill, attendance total, share picture, reminders.
risks.mitigation: Give sessions an explicit status; keep cancelled and moved-away sessions out of StudentSchedule items and out of headline, clash, attendance and reminder logic; draw them only as display ghosts.

risks.risk: Old cached app versions and the offline timetable copy do not know the new change list. If the server stops excluding a cancelled date so the new app can grey it, old clients show the class as normal.
risks.mitigation: Keep sending the original date in excludedDates and send the Cancelled or Moved record in a separate list the new client uses to draw the ghost; refetch when the app comes to the front.

risks.risk: A sync glitch (blank time skipped by the fetcher, short sections table) looks like the university dropped a session or section: the teacher gets a false 'your change was dropped', hand-added links vanish, and the returning section is a new row.
risks.mitigation: Show staff the teacher changes a sync will drop before Apply; reconcile inside the apply transaction; keep text snapshots so links re-attach by course code + section number and the log survives.

risks.risk: Instructor text changes silently move powers: a reassignment hands the section to whoever carries the new name; a re-spelling empties a teacher's timetable; a typo by RSA in the section editor attaches or detaches classes. Names are compared three different ways in the code today.
risks.mitigation: One name-normalising function used everywhere; record old and new instructor at apply time; alert both teachers; flag probable re-spellings to staff for a one-tap confirm; never re-link automatically.
